attrs\n    }\n\n    /// Attrs for the text label inside a branch.\n    pub fn branch_text_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap { part_only_attrs(&Part::BranchText) }\n\n    /// Attrs for the children container inside an expanded branch (`role=\"group\"`).\n    pub fn branch_content_attrs(&self, node_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = part_only_attrs(&Part::BranchContent { node_id: Key::default() });\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"group\");\n        if !self.is_node_expanded(node_id) { attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Hidden, true); }\n        attrs\n    }\n\n    /// Attrs for a leaf node. When `has_children` is set, `aria-expanded` is\n    /// emitted so screen readers announce the affordance; `href` renders `<a>`.\n    pub fn leaf_attrs(&self, node_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = part_only_attrs(&Part::Leaf { node_id: Key::default() });\n        let node = self.ctx.items.get(node_id);\n        let is_selected = self.is_node_selected(node_id);\n        let is_focused  = self.is_node_focused(node_id);\n        let is_expanded = self.is_node_expanded(node_id);\n        let level = node.map_or(1, |n| n.level as u32 + 1);\n        let (setsize, posinset) = self.sibling_info(node_id);\n        let item = node.and_then(|n| n.value.as_ref());\n        let disabled = item.is_some_and(|v| v.disabled);\n        let has_children_flag = item.is_some_and(|v| v.has_children);\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Id, node_dom_id(&self.ctx.ids, node_id));\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"treeitem\");\n        if has_children_flag {\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Expanded), bool_token(is_expanded));\n        }\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Selected), bool_token(is_selected));\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Level), level.to_string());\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::SetSize), setsize.to_string());\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::PosInSet), posinset.to_string());\n        self.apply_node_state(&mut attrs, disabled, is_selected, is_expanded, is_focused, node_id);\n        if let Some(href) = self.node_href(node_id) { attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Href, href); }\n        attrs\n    }\n\n    /// Handle activation of a leaf node: select and focus.\n    pub fn on_leaf_click(&self, node_id: &Key) {\n        (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone()));\n        (self.send)(Event::FocusNode(node_id.clone()));\n    }\n\n    /// Attrs for the text label inside a leaf node.\n    pub fn leaf_text_attrs(&self) -> AttrMap { part_only_attrs(&Part::LeafText) }\n\n    /// Attrs for a node's drag handle (`role=\"button\"`, localized `aria-label`).\n    pub fn drag_handle_attrs(&self, node_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = part_only_attrs(&Part::DragHandle { node_id: Key::default() });\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"button\");\n        let label = self.ctx.items.get(node_id).and_then(|n| n.value.as_ref())\n            .map_or(\"\", |v| v.label.as_str());\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), (self.ctx.messages.drag_handle_label)(label, &self.ctx.locale));\n        if self.is_dragging(node_id) { attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Grabbed), \"true\"); }\n        attrs\n    }\n\n    /// Attrs for the drop indicator at the current drop target.\n    pub fn drop_indicator_attrs(&self, target: &CollectionDropTarget) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = part_only_attrs(&Part::DropIndicator);\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Hidden), \"true\");\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-drop-position\"), target.position.to_string());\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-drop-target\"), node_dom_id(&self.ctx.ids, &target.key));\n        attrs\n    }\n\n    /// Map a keydown on the tree root (active descendant `node_id`) to events\n    /// per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern (§3.2). Logical, not RTL-swapped (§3.3).\n    pub fn on_node_keydown(&self, node_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData) {\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::FocusNext),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::FocusPrev),\n            KeyboardKey::Home => (self.send)(Event::FocusFirst),\n            KeyboardKey::End => (self.send)(Event::FocusLast),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => {\n                if self.is_branch(node_id) && !self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {\n                    (self.send)(Event::ExpandNode(node_id.clone()));\n                } else {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusNext);\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {\n                if self.is_branch(node_id) && self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {\n                    (self.send)(Event::CollapseNode(node_id.clone()));\n                } else {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusParent);\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::Enter | KeyboardKey::Space => (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone())),\n            _ => if let Some(ch) = data.character {\n                if ch == '*' { self.expand_siblings(node_id); }\n                else if !ch.is_control() { (self.send)(Event::TypeaheadSearch(ch)); }\n            },\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Keyboard drag-and-drop protocol on a drag handle: Enter/Space pickup or\n    /// confirm, Arrow Up/Down step the target, Escape cancels.\n    pub fn on_drag_handle_keydown(&self, node_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData) {\n        if !self.props.dnd_enabled { return; }\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::Enter | KeyboardKey::Space => {\n                if self.is_dragging(node_id) { (self.send)(Event::Drop); }\n                else { (self.send)(Event::DragStart(node_id.clone())); }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown if self.is_dragging(node_id) => (self.send)(Event::DragMoveNext),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp if self.is_dragging(node_id) => (self.send)(Event::DragMovePrev),\n            KeyboardKey::Escape if self.is_dragging(node_id) => (self.send)(Event::CancelDrag),\n            _ => {}\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Move the focus indicator to a node.\n    pub fn focus_node(&self, node_id: &Key) { (self.send)(Event::FocusNode(node_id.clone())); }\n\n    /// Expand all expandable nodes.\n    pub fn expand_all(&self) { (self.send)(Event::ExpandAll); }\n\n    /// Collapse all nodes.\n    pub fn collapse_all(&self) { (self.send)(Event::CollapseAll); }\n\n    /// Whether the node renders as an expandable branch (real or lazy children).\n    fn is_branch(&self, node_id: &Key) -> bool {\n        self.ctx.items.get(node_id)\n            .is_some_and(|n| n.has_children || n.value.as_ref().is_some_and(|v| v.has_children))\n    }\n\n    /// Expand every expandable sibling of `node_id` (the `*` shortcut).\n    fn expand_siblings(&self, node_id: &Key) {\n        let parent = self.ctx.items.get(node_id).and_then(|n| n.parent_key.clone());\n        let siblings = match &parent {\n            Some(parent) => self.ctx.items.children_of(parent).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n            None => self.ctx.items.all_nodes().filter(|n| n.parent_key.is_none()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),\n        };\n        for sibling in siblings {\n            if sibling.has_children { (self.send)(Event::ExpandNode(sibling.key.clone())); }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// The node's navigation href, if any.\n    fn node_href(&self, node_id: &Key) -> Option<&str> {\n        self.ctx.items.get(node_id).and_then(|n| n.value.as_ref()).and_then(|v| v.href.as_deref())\n    }\n\n    /// Apply the shared `data-ars-*` / dnd state markers for branch and leaf.\n    fn apply_node_state(&self, attrs: &mut AttrMap, disabled: bool, is_selected: bool,\n        is_expanded: bool, is_focused: bool, node_id: &Key) {\n        if disabled {\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), \"true\");\n            attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-disabled\"), true);\n        }\n        if is_selected { attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-selected\"), true); }\n        if is_expanded { attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-expanded\"), true); }\n        if is_focused && self.ctx.focus_visible { attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-focus-visible\"), true); }\n        if self.props.dnd_enabled {\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::RoleDescription), \"draggable\");\n            if self.is_dragging(node_id) { attrs.set_bool(HtmlAttr::Data(\"ars-dragging\"), true); }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// `\"true\"`/`\"false\"` ARIA boolean token.\nconst fn bool_token(value: bool) -> &'static str { if value { \"true\" } else { \"false\" } }\n\n/// An `AttrMap` carrying only a part's scope/part data attributes.\nfn part_only_attrs(part: &Part) -> AttrMap {\n    let mut attrs = AttrMap::new();\n    let [(scope_attr, scope_val), (part_attr, part_val)] = part.data_attrs();\n    attrs.set(scope_attr, scope_val).set(part_attr, part_val);\n    attrs\n}\n\n/// The stable DOM id for a tree node, used for `aria-activedescendant` and the\n/// node element's `id`.\nfn node_dom_id(ids: &ComponentIds, key: &Key) -> String {\n    ids.item(\"node\", &dom_safe_key_token(key))\n}\n\nimpl ConnectApi for Api<'_> {\n    type Part = Part;\n\n    fn part_attrs(&self, part: Part) -> AttrMap {\n        match part {\n            Part::Root => self.root_attrs(),\n            Part::Branch { ref node_id } => self.branch_attrs(node_id),\n            Part::BranchControl { ref node_id } => self.branch_control_attrs(node_id),\n            Part::BranchIndicator { ref node_id } => self.branch_indicator_attrs(node_id),\n            Part::BranchText => self.branch_text_attrs(),\n            Part::BranchContent { ref node_id } => self.branch_content_attrs(node_id),\n            Part::Leaf { ref node_id } => self.leaf_attrs(node_id),\n            Part::LeafText => self.leaf_text_attrs(),\n            Part::DragHandle { ref node_id } => self.drag_handle_attrs(node_id),\n            Part::DropIndicator => self.ctx.drop_target.as_ref()\n                .map_or_else(|| part_only_attrs(&Part::DropIndicator), |t| self.drop_indicator_attrs(t)),\n        }\n    }\n}\n```"

1091	
1092	> **Drag and Drop Reorder**: When `dnd_enabled: true` is set, TreeView surfaces the agnostic drag-and-drop reorder logic — the `DragHandle` and `DropIndicator` anatomy parts (canonical bare names, per `06-collections.md` §10.8 and the listbox/gridlist/table specs), the drag-state events, valid drop-slot enumeration, cycle-free drop validation, and `ReorderEvent` path computation. It reports completion through `Props::on_reorder` driven by the named `Effect::Reorder`. Dropping **between** siblings uses `DropPosition::Before`/`After`; dropping **onto** a node to reparent uses `DropPosition::On`. The collection-level `DraggableCollection<T>` / `DroppableCollection<T>` trait impls (which bundle the live `selection::State`), pointer hit-testing, the 500 ms hover-expand timer, and `use_drag`/`use_drop` DOM wiring are **adapter** concerns (tracked by the TreeView Leptos/Dioxus adapter tasks), not part of this agnostic core.
1093	
1094	### 4.2 Drag-Reorder Behavior
1095	
1096	When drag-and-drop reorder is enabled (`dnd_enabled: true`), the following behaviors apply:
1097	
1098	- **Drag handle**: Each tree item renders an optional drag handle affordance (the `drag::Handle` anatomy part). The handle is the grab target; the entire row is not draggable by default to avoid conflicts with text selection.
1099	- **Hover-expand**: When dragging over a collapsed tree node, the node automatically expands after a 500ms hover delay. This allows users to drop items into nested levels without manually expanding first.
1100	- **Drop target indication**: Valid drop zones are visually highlighted during drag. Three drop positions are supported:
1101	  - `Before` — insert before the target node (horizontal line above)
1102	  - `After` — insert after the target node (horizontal line below)
1103	  - `Child` — insert as a child of the target node (target node background highlight)
1104	- **Drop position detection**: The drop position is determined by the pointer's vertical position within the target row: top 25% = `Before`, bottom 25% = `After`, middle 50% = `Child`.
1105	- **Keyboard drag**: Full keyboard support for reordering:
1106	  - `Enter` or `Space` on a focused drag handle to pick up the item
1107	  - Arrow keys to move the item through valid drop positions
1108	  - `Enter` to confirm the drop
1109	  - `Escape` to cancel and return the item to its original position
1110	- **Reorder callback**: `on_reorder: Callback<ReorderEvent>` fires when a drop is completed.
1111	
1112	```rust
1113	/// Event emitted when a tree item is reordered via drag-and-drop.
1114	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
1115	pub struct ReorderEvent {
1116	    /// Path of the dragged item (sequence of keys from root to item).
1117	    pub source_path: Vec<Key>,
1118	    /// Path of the drop target.
1119	    pub target_path: Vec<Key>,
1120	    /// Where relative to the target the item was dropped.
1121	    pub position: DropPosition,
1122	}
1123	
1124	// `DropPosition` — defined in `06-collections.md`
1125	```

1127	## 5. Variant: Lazy Loading
1128	
1129	`TreeView` supports lazy loading of child nodes for large or server-driven hierarchies. When a node is first expanded and its children are not yet loaded, the machine fires a `LoadChildren` event.
1130

1134	/// The load_children callback is registered in the adapter layer, not in Props.
1135	/// When provided, nodes without pre-loaded children will trigger lazy loading on expand.
1136	/// The adapter observes `LoadChildren(Key)` events and calls the user-provided callback.
1137	```
1138	
1139	```rust
1140	/// Type alias for the lazy-load callback.
1141	/// The adapter calls this with the parent node's key when children need loading.
1142	/// The callback should eventually send a `ChildrenLoaded` event back to the machine.
1143	/// Uses `Rc` so the adapter can clone it into event handler closures.
1144	pub type LoadChildrenFn = Rc<dyn Fn(Key)>;
1145	```

  "new_string": "When drag-and-drop reorder is enabled (`dnd_enabled: true`), the following behaviors apply. The\n**agnostic core** owns the data-model logic (slot enumeration, validity, paths, attrs, keyboard\nprotocol); pointer hit-testing and the hover-expand timer are **adapter**-resolved.\n\n- **Drag handle**: Each tree item renders an optional drag handle affordance (the `DragHandle`\n  anatomy part). The handle is the grab target; the entire row is not draggable by default to\n  avoid conflicts with text selection. `drag_handle_attrs` emits `role=\"button\"` and a localized\n  `aria-label` from `Messages::drag_handle_label`, plus `aria-grabbed=\"true\"` while dragging.\n- **Hover-expand** (adapter): When the pointer dwells over a collapsed node during a drag, the\n  adapter expands it after a 500 ms hover delay by sending `ExpandNode`. The agnostic core has no\n  timer.\n- **Drop target indication**: The `DropIndicator` part marks the current drop slot with\n  `data-ars-drop-position` (`before` / `on` / `after`) and `data-ars-drop-target` (the target\n  node's id). Three drop positions are supported:\n  - `DropPosition::Before` — insert before the target node (horizontal line above)\n  - `DropPosition::After` — insert after the target node (horizontal line below)\n  - `DropPosition::On` — reparent as a child of the target node (target background highlight)\n- **Drop position detection** (adapter): The adapter maps the pointer's vertical position within\n  the target row — top 25% = `Before`, bottom 25% = `After`, middle 50% = `On` — to a\n  `CollectionDropTarget` and sends `DragOver`.\n- **Keyboard drag** (agnostic core, via `on_drag_handle_keydown`):\n  - `Enter` / `Space` on a focused drag handle picks up the item (`DragStart`).\n  - Arrow Up/Down step the item through the valid drop slots (`DragMovePrev` / `DragMoveNext`).\n  - `Enter` confirms the drop (`Drop`).\n  - `Escape` cancels and discards the drop target (`CancelDrag`).\n- **Drop validity**: The core rejects dropping a node onto itself or any of its descendants\n  (cycle prevention) in both `DragOver` and `Drop`.\n- **Reorder callback**: `Props::on_reorder: Option<Callback<ReorderEvent>>` fires when a drop is\n  completed. The core never mutates `ctx.items`; the consumer applies the reorder to its data\n  source and re-supplies props (pure-notification, like Tabs).\n\n```rust\n/// Event emitted when a tree node is reordered via drag-and-drop.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ReorderEvent {\n    /// Path of the dragged node (sequence of keys from root to node).\n    pub source_path: Vec<Key>,\n    /// Path of the drop target.\n    pub target_path: Vec<Key>,\n    /// Where relative to the target the node was dropped.\n    pub position: DropPosition,\n}\n\n// `DropPosition` and `CollectionDropTarget` — defined in `ars_collections::dnd`\n// (`06-collections.md` §10). 950	```text
951	TreeView
952	└── Root                           role="tree"
953	    ├── Branch                     role="treeitem" aria-expanded
954	    │   ├── BranchControl        (clickable row; <a> when href present)
955	    │   │   ├── BranchIndicator  aria-hidden="true"
956	    │   │   └── BranchText
957	    │   └── BranchContent        role="group"
958	    │       └── (nested Branch or Leaf nodes)
959	    └── Leaf                       role="treeitem" (aria-expanded when has_children)
960	        └── LeafText             (<a> when href present)
961	```
962	
963	| Part              | Element                               | Key Attributes                                                                                                                                                                                              |
964	| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
965	| `Root`            | `<ul>` or `<div>`                     | `data-ars-scope="tree-view"`, `data-ars-part="root"`, `role="tree"`, `aria-multiselectable`                                                                                                                 |
966	| `Branch`          | `<li>` or `<div>`                     | `role="treeitem"`, `aria-expanded` (also set when `has_children` is true with no loaded children), `aria-selected`, `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`, `data-ars-expanded`, `data-ars-selected` |
967	| `BranchControl`   | `<div>` or `<a>` (when href)          | `data-ars-scope="tree-view"`, `data-ars-part="branch-control"`, `href` (when present)                                                                                                                       |
968	| `BranchIndicator` | `<span>`                              | `data-ars-scope="tree-view"`, `data-ars-part="branch-indicator"`, `aria-hidden="true"`, `data-ars-expanded`                                                                                                 |
969	| `BranchText`      | `<span>`                              | `data-ars-scope="tree-view"`, `data-ars-part="branch-text"`                                                                                                                                                 |
970	| `BranchContent`   | `<ul>` or `<div>`                     | `role="group"`, `data-ars-scope="tree-view"`, `data-ars-part="branch-content"`                                                                                                                              |
971	| `Leaf`            | `<li>`, `<div>`, or `<a>` (when href) | `role="treeitem"`, `aria-expanded="false"` (when `has_children` is true), `aria-selected`, `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`, `data-ars-selected`, `href` (when present)                        |
972	| `LeafText`        | `<span>`                              | `data-ars-scope="tree-view"`, `data-ars-part="leaf-text"`                                                                                                                                                   |

1051	
1052	### 3.6 Expand/Collapse Keyboard Navigation Race Conditions
1053	
1054	Rapid keyboard interactions on `TreeView` nodes can cause race conditions between expand/collapse animations and focus movement:
1055	
1056	1. **Debounce Expansion**: Expand/collapse transitions are not debounced — each ArrowRight (expand) or ArrowLeft (collapse) takes effect immediately. However, the focus movement that follows expansion (ArrowRight on expanded node moves focus to first child) waits until the children are actually rendered.
1057	2. **Pending Expansion Guard**: If ArrowRight is pressed on a collapsed node, the node enters an "expanding" state. A second ArrowRight during this state is queued and executed after children render (moving focus to the first child), rather than being ignored.
1058	3. **Collapse During Focus-In-Child**: If ArrowLeft collapses a parent while focus is on a child, focus moves to the parent node before the collapse animation starts. The adapter must move focus synchronously, then animate the collapse.
1059	4. **Async Children**: For lazily-loaded children (`on_expand` triggers async fetch), the node shows a loading indicator and expansion completes when children arrive. ArrowRight during loading is a no-op.
1060	
```

1048	### 3.5 Scroll Into View
1049	
1050	When focus moves to an off-screen tree item, the adapter scrolls it into view using `element.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', inline: 'nearest' })`. For nested scrollable containers, the adapter must walk up the DOM and call `scrollIntoView` on the closest scrollable ancestor only. On iOS Safari, where programmatic focus doesn't trigger scroll, the adapter must explicitly call `scrollIntoView` after `element.focus()`. Smooth scrolling is avoided for keyboard navigation to prevent timing conflicts.

For nested scrollable containers, the adapter must walk up the DOM and call `scrollIntoView` on the closest scrollable ancestor only. On iOS Safari, where programmatic focus doesn't trigger scroll, the adapter must explicitly call `scrollIntoView`. Smooth scrolling is avoided for keyboard navigation to prevent timing conflicts."

1	//! `spec compile-snippets` — parse Rust code blocks in spec markdown
2	//! through `syn::parse_file` and surface syntax errors.
3	//!
4	//! ## What this catches
5	//!
6	//! - Top-level Rust syntax bugs in spec snippets: missing braces,
7	//!   mistyped `pub fn`, unterminated string literals, unbalanced
8	//!   generics outside macro bodies, etc.
9	//! - Coverage across the full spec corpus —
10	//!   `spec/{components,foundation,leptos-components,dioxus-components,shared,testing}/`.
11	//!   The pre-existing `lint-code` linter only walked
12	//!   `spec/components/` and never invoked a Rust parser, so foundation
13	//!   and per-adapter specs had zero parse coverage.
14	//!
15	//! ## What this **does not** catch (important — read this)
16	//!
17	//! - **Macro-internal syntax.** `view! { … }` and `rsx! { … }` are
18	//!   opaque token trees to both `syn` and `rustc`; everything inside
19	//!   the outer braces is unchecked. The original Leptos `view!`
20	//!   regression (an inline `|errors: ArcRwSignal<Errors>|` closure
21	//!   where the macro parser misread `<Errors>` as an HTML tag) sits
22	//!   *inside* the macro and would not be caught here. The unit test
23	//!   suites at `crates/ars-{leptos,dioxus}/tests/` are the source of
24	//!   truth for macro-internal correctness.
25	//! - **Type / path resolution.** A snippet that names a type defined
26	//!   nowhere in the workspace still parses syntactically. Use
27	//!   `cargo check` against a fixture crate for that.
28	//! - **Borrow-checker / ownership errors.** Same as above —
29	//!   `syn::parse_file` is purely a parser.
30	//!
31	//! ## Opting out
32	//!
33	//! Code blocks that intentionally contain partial or pseudo-Rust
34	//! (signatures shown for documentation purposes, top-level expressions
35	//! meant to live inside an outer fn body, etc.) opt out by tagging the
36	//! fence info-string with `rust,no_check` (also recognised:
37	//! `rust,ignore`, `rust,no_run`, mirroring rustdoc). The extractor
38	//! honors those markers and skips the block.
39	//!
40	//! ## Performance
41	//!
42	//! Fast: no compiler invocation. Runs in milliseconds across all 2000+
43	//! Rust blocks in the spec, so it is suitable for inclusion in the
44	//! `cargo xci` pipeline (see `xtask::ci::Step::SpecCompileSnippets`).
45	
46	use std::{fs, path::Path};
47	
48	use crate::manifest::{Error, SpecRoot};
49	
50	/// CLI entry point.
51	///
52	/// Always returns `Ok(String)`. The text either begins with `ok:` (no
53	/// findings) or with `N finding(s):` followed by per-finding lines.
54	///
55	/// When `fix` is `true`, each failing block has its opening fence rewritten
56	/// from `` ```rust `` (or `` ```rs ``) to `` ```rust,no_check `` (or
57	/// `` ```rs,no_check ``) in place; the file is rewritten on disk and the
58	/// returned text reports how many fences were patched.
59	///
60	/// # Errors
61	///
62	/// Returns [`Error::Io`] when a target file cannot be read or written.
63	pub fn execute(root: &SpecRoot, fix: bool) -> Result<String, Error> {
64	    let mut files = Vec::new();
65	
66	    for sub in [
67	        "components",
68	        "foundation",
69	        "leptos-components",
70	        "dioxus-components",
71	        "shared",
72	        "testing",
73	    ] {
74	        let dir = root.path.join(sub);
75	
76	        collect_md_files(&dir, &mut files).map_err(Error::Io)?;
77	    }
78	
79	    files.sort();
80	
81	    let display_root = fs::canonicalize(&root.path).unwrap_or_else(|_| root.path.clone());
82	
83	    let mut findings = Vec::new();
84	    let mut blocks_checked = 0usize;
85	    let mut fences_patched = 0usize;
86	
87	    for path in &files {
88	        let source = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(Error::Io)?;
89	
90	        let display = path
91	            .strip_prefix(&display_root)
92	            .unwrap_or(path)
93	            .display()
94	            .to_string();
95	
96	        let blocks = extract_rust_blocks(&source);
97	
98	        let mut failing_fence_lines = Vec::new();
99	
100	        for block in &blocks {
101	            blocks_checked += 1;
102	
103	            if let Some(message) = check_block(block) {
104	                findings.push(Finding {
105	                    file: display.clone(),
106	                    line: block.start_line,
107	                    message,
108	                });
109	
110	                if fix {
111	                    // The fence line is one above the block's first content line.
112	                    failing_fence_lines.push(block.start_line.saturating_sub(1));
113	                }
114	            }
115	        }
116	
117	        if fix && !failing_fence_lines.is_empty() {
118	            let patched = rewrite_fences_to_no_check(&source, &failing_fence_lines);
119	
120	            if patched != source {
121	                let count = patched_fence_count(&source, &patched);
122	
123	                fences_patched += count;
124	
125	                fs::write(path, patched).map_err(Error::Io)?;
126	            }
127	        }
128	    }
129	
130	    let mut out = String::new();
```

    fn sync_controlled_value_updates_state_and_bindable_value() {

        assert_eq!(*service.state(), State::Open { item: key("blog") });
        assert_eq!(service.context().value.get(), &Some(key("blog")));
        assert_eq!(service.context().previous_item, Some(key("docs")));

        drop(service.send(Event::SyncControlledValue(None)));

        assert_eq!(*service.state(), State::Idle);
        assert_eq!(service.context().value.get(), &None);
        assert_eq!(service.context().previous_item, Some(key("blog")));
    }

=== AGENTS.md remaining mutation-as-gate references ===
29:7. **MANDATORY:** Invoke the `post-implementation-audit` skill (`.agents/skills/post-implementation-audit/SKILL.md`). It runs three sequential audits on the new code — (a) spec/implementation drift with "best outcome" recommendations, (b) iterative "anything else missing?" passes (minimum two rounds), (c) test-coverage audit across every test type the workspace uses (unit, snapshot, proptest, mutation, doc, spec-conformance, llvm-cov). **Every finding lands in _this_ PR — no deferral, no follow-up issues.** This step exists because initial implementations consistently ship spec drift and silent contract violations that take 3+ review round-trips to surface; the audit collapses them into one. Skipping this step is a contract violation.
123:**Mutation testing is NOT a pre-PR requisite for agnostic component work.** Do not run a targeted `cargo xmutants` pass as a delivery/audit gate, and do not block a PR on a clean local mutation run. Surviving (`MISSED`) mutants are surfaced by the Nightly CI `mutation-testing` job (see below); triage them — add tests for real gaps, or add a justified line-agnostic `.cargo/mutants.toml` exclude for true equivalent mutations — in a dedicated follow-up when Nightly reports them, not during initial component delivery. (Running a local mutation pass voluntarily is fine, but it is never required and never blocks delivery or review.)
137:**Adding a new state machine inside an existing crate requires no CI changes** — its mutations land in whichever shard the cargo-mutants partitioner places them. The shard counts are sized so the slowest runner stays well under 30 minutes today and under ~50 minutes at the planned endpoint; re-balance only when a crate outgrows that budget (visible on the nightly dashboard as one shard pulling away from the others).
141:**Excluded crates** (mutation testing's signal degrades wherever determinism does): adapter glue (`ars-leptos`, `ars-dioxus`), DOM/FFI (`ars-dom`), ICU/FFI (`ars-i18n`), test infrastructure (`ars-test-harness*`), and the proc-macro crate (`ars-derive`, runs in the compiler). Adding a brand-new crate that is a good mutation target requires one new matrix entry; run a local scout first (`cargo mutants -p <crate> --list` to size, then a real run) so we know the right shard count before the nightly fires.

=== post-implementation-audit SKILL.md mutation requirements ===
10:The skill is mandatory per CLAUDE.md "Development Workflow" step 7 — run it after implementing any user-requested task (feature, bug fix, refactor) and before presenting the final result for user review.
110:- **`.cargo/mutants.toml`** — are any new equivalent mutations documented with justifications? (Phase 3 will validate this; surface it here if a mutation that *should* be equivalent isn't documented yet.)
129:By this point the code is convention-aligned and well-specced. Now check the **test surface** — both depth (line / branch / mutation coverage) and breadth (does every test type that *should* exist for this kind of change exist?).
142:| **Mutation tests** (`cargo xmutants`) | Tests that *exist* but don't actually constrain behavior | Run `cargo xmutants -p <crate> -f <file>` and triage every `MISSED`; this is mandatory for every new or materially changed framework-agnostic component. Prefer `cargo xmutants` over bare `cargo mutants` — it applies the same per-crate `--features` profile as Nightly CI (for example `ars-components/i18n`) so snapshot and i18n-gated tests match CI. |
144:| **Spec-conformance tests** | Anatomy drift between spec and impl | Check `crates/ars-components/tests/spec_conformance/*.rs` for an entry covering the new component's `Part` enum and public API/attribute contract; this is mandatory for every new framework-agnostic component |
196:   cargo xmutants -p <crate> -f <file>
200:   cargo xmutants -p ars-components -f crates/ars-components/src/<category>/<component>/mod.rs
202:   Use the actual file path for single-file modules. Prefer `cargo xmutants` over bare `cargo mutants` — the xtask wrapper applies the Nightly CI feature profile (for example `ars-components/i18n`) so local runs do not fail on snapshot or i18n-gated code paths that plain `cargo mutants` misses.
204:   For each `MISSED` line, decide:
205:   - **Real test gap** → add a test that kills the mutation (often a positive-direction assertion the existing tests skipped).
206:   - **Equivalent mutation** → add a regex to `.cargo/mutants.toml` `exclude_re` with a written justification explaining *why* the mutation cannot change observable behavior.

216:The targeted `cargo xmutants` run is a pre-PR implementation/audit requirement. After the PR is opened, agents **MUST NOT** rerun mutation tests during Codex review rounds unless the user explicitly asks for another mutation run.

234:The goal is **not** "100% line coverage at any cost". The goal is *"no surviving mutations, no unreachable defensive code, every test type that should exist does exist"*. A 99% line-coverage report with all mutations caught is a stronger position than a 100% line-coverage report with three surviving mutations. If the last 1% of uncovered code is a genuinely unreachable defensive guard, document it in `mutants.toml` and move on.

file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:520  (commentId=3311244547)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Honor multiple=true in selection state**

With only `Props::multiple(true)`, `root_attrs` advertises `aria-multiselectable` via `ctx.multiple`, but the selection machine is still initialized from `props.selection_mode` (default `Single`). In that documented setup selecting a second node replaces the first, so multiple selection does not actually work unless callers also know to set `selection_mode(Multiple)`; derive the effective mode from `multiple` before constructing the selection state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FHeHm
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:790  (commentId=3311244552)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Sync selection configuration prop changes**

When `Service::set_props` changes `multiple`, `selection_mode`, or `selection_behavior`, this predicate returns no `SyncProps` because those fields are ignored; even if another prop happens to trigger `SyncProps`, the handler never copies those fields into `ctx`. In dynamic prop scenarios such as switching a tree from single to multiple selection or disabling selection, the root attributes and selection transitions keep using the stale configuration from initialization.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FHeHv
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1428  (commentId=3311244561)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make Space toggle selected nodes off**

In multiple-selection `Toggle` mode, pressing Space on an already-selected node currently sends only `SelectNode`; `selection::State::select` inserts or retains keys, so the key is never removed. This violates the TreeView keyboard contract that Space toggles the focused node in multiple mode and leaves keyboard users without a way to deselect through the normal keyboard interaction.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FHeH3
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1411  (commentId=3311244570)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not move right from leaf nodes**

For a focused leaf, the Right Arrow should be inert because there is no child to enter, but this fallback sends `FocusNext`, so focus advances to the next visible node and can even wrap to the first node at the end of the tree. That breaks the documented tree keyboard semantics and makes leaf navigation differ from the ARIA tree pattern.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FHeH9
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:651  (commentId=3311244579)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Expand lazy branches in bulk expansion**

This only expands nodes with loaded children, but the component treats `TreeItem::has_children` as an expandable lazy branch elsewhere. Calling `expand_all()` on a tree with unloaded lazy children leaves those branches collapsed, so consumers cannot trigger their lazy-load expansion through the bulk command; use the same branch predicate that includes the item-level `has_children` flag.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear stale focus when items change**

When `items` is replaced with a collection that no longer contains the focused key, `SyncProps` updates `ctx.items` but leaves `ctx.focused_node` untouched. Until the next focus movement, `root_attrs` emits `aria-activedescendant` for an element id that no longer exists, which leaves assistive tech with a broken active-descendant reference after removals or reorders that drop the focused node.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FHeIG
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:810  (commentId=3311244591)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep pointer clicks from forcing focus-visible**

Because every `FocusNode` plan unconditionally sets `focus_visible = true`, the pointer click handlers (`on_leaf_click` and `on_branch_control_click`) also render `data-ars-focus-visible` after a mouse/touch activation. In pointer-focus scenarios this shows keyboard-only focus styling even though `Focus { is_keyboard: false }` was designed to suppress it; preserve the current modality instead of always forcing the keyboard-visible state.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FHeIN
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:692  (commentId=3311244601)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject drop targets that are not tree nodes**

During pointer DnD, an adapter can send a stale or otherwise invalid target key; the current validity check only rejects self/descendant targets, so an unknown key is accepted and `Drop` later emits a reorder event whose `target_path` is just that nonexistent key. Require `target.key` to exist in `ctx.items` before storing it as the active drop target.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep focus visible after collapsing ancestors**

If the focused node is inside a branch that is collapsed via `CollapseNode`, `ToggleNode`, or `CollapseAll`, the expansion set changes but `focused_node` can keep pointing at a now-hidden descendant. The root then keeps emitting `aria-activedescendant` for an element that adapters no longer render, so collapse operations should move focus to the collapsed ancestor or clear it when the active node becomes hidden.

**<sub><sub>![P3 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P3-lightgrey?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match typeahead against the displayed label**

`TreeItem::label` is the display label used by the component, but typeahead searches `Node::text_value` instead. When consumers build a collection whose `text_value` differs from the shown label (for example after a label update or when using a separate search token), typing the visible first letter will not focus the item; use the stored `TreeItem.label` with a fallback to `text_value`.

851	/// Find the next visible node whose label starts with `ch` (case-insensitive),
852	/// searching after the focused node and wrapping around.
853	fn typeahead_target(ctx: &Context, ch: char) -> Option<Key> {
854	    let needle = ch.to_lowercase().next().unwrap_or(ch);

860	    }
861

863	        .focused_node
864	        .as_ref()
865	        .and_then(|focused| visible.iter().position(|key| key == focused))
866	        .map_or(0, |pos| pos + 1);
867	
868	    visible
869	        .iter()
870	        .cycle()
871	        .skip(start)
872	        .take(visible.len())
873	        .find(|key| {
874	            ctx.items
875	                .get(key)
876	                .and_then(|node| node.text_value.chars().next())
877	                .map(|first| first.to_lowercase().next().unwrap_or(first))
878	                == Some(needle)
879	        })
880	        .cloned()
881	}

886	/// it (which would create a cycle), three slots are produced in reading order:
887	/// `Before`, `On` (reparent), then `After`. Keyboard stepping cycles through
888	/// this list.
889	fn valid_drop_slots(ctx: &Context, dragging: &Key) -> Vec<CollectionDropTarget> {
890	    let mut slots = Vec::new();
891	
892	    for key in visible_keys(ctx) {

894	            continue;
895	        }
896	
897	        slots.extend(
898	            [DropPosition::Before, DropPosition::On, DropPosition::After].map(|position| {
899	                CollectionDropTarget {
900	                    key: key.clone(),
901	                    position,
902	                }
903	            }),

920	    let dragging = ctx.dragging.as_ref()?;
921

923	
924	    if slots.is_empty() {

937	    } else {

940	            Direction::Prev => slots.len() - 1,

  "new_string": "#[test]\nfn collapsing_ancestor_clamps_focus_to_that_ancestor() {\n    // Focus a descendant, then collapse its parent: focus must move up to the\n    // now-collapsed ancestor so aria-activedescendant stays on a rendered node.\n    let mut service = service(props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNode(key(2)))); // Apple (under Fruits)\n    drop(service.send(Event::CollapseNode(key(1)))); // hides Apple\n\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(1))); // clamped to Fruits\n\n    // And navigation proceeds correctly from the clamped position.\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNext));\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(4))); // Vegetables\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn collapse_all_clamps_focus_to_root_ancestor() {\n    let mut service = service(props());\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNode(key(3)))); // Banana (under Fruits)\n    drop(service.send(Event::CollapseAll));\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(1))); // Fruits (root)\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn sync_props_clears_focus_when_focused_node_removed() {\n    let mut service = service(props());\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNode(key(7)))); // Grains\n    // New collection without Grains.\n    let trimmed = TreeCollection::new(vec![branch(1, \"Fruits\", true, vec![leaf(2, \"Apple\")])]);\n    drop(service.set_props(props().items(trimmed)));\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, None);\n}"
}

// single mode\n    drop(service.send(Event::SelectNode(key(2))));\n\n    drop(service.set_props(props().multiple(true))); // switch to multiple\n    drop(service.send(Event::SelectNode(key(3))));\n\n    let api = service.connect(&|_| {});\n    assert!(\n        api.is_node_selected(&key(2)) && api.is_node_selected(&key(3)),\n        \"after switching to multiple at runtime, both nodes stay selected\"\n    );\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn set_props_switch_to_none_stops_selection() {\n    let mut service = service(props().selected(selection::Set::Single(key(2))));\n    drop(service.set_props(\n        props()\n            .selected(selection::Set::Single(key(2)))\n            .selection_mode(selection::Mode::None),\n    ));\n    // In None mode further selection is rejected.\n    let result = service.send(Event::SelectNode(key(3)));\n    assert!(!result.context_changed);\n    assert!(!service.connect(&|_| {}).is_node_selected(&key(3)));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn expand_all_expands_lazy_branches() {\n    // A node with the has_children flag but no loaded children is a lazy\n    // branch; ExpandAll must expand it so consumers can trigger lazy loading.\n    let items = TreeCollection::new(vec![leaf_with(\n        9,\n        \"Lazy\",\n        TreeItem {\n            has_children: true,\n            ..item(\"Lazy\")\n        },\n    )]);\n    let mut service = service(props().items(items));\n    drop(service.send(Event::ExpandAll));\n    assert!(service.context().expanded.get().contains(&key(9)));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn drag_over_rejects_unknown_target_key() {\n    let mut service = service(dnd_props());\n    drop(service.send(Event::DragStart(key(2))));\n    let result = service.send(Event::DragOver(CollectionDropTarget {\n        key: key(999), // not a node in the collection\n        position: DropPosition::On,\n    }));\n    assert!(!result.context_changed);\n    assert!(service.context().drop_target.is_none());\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn typeahead_matches_displayed_label_not_text_value() {\n    // text_value differs from the displayed label; typing the label's first\n    // letter must focus the node.\n    let labeled = TreeItemConfig {\n        key: key(1),\n        text_value: \"zzz\".to_string(),\n        value: TreeItem {\n            label: \"Apple\".to_string(),\n            ..TreeItem::default()\n        },\n        children: Vec::new(),\n        default_expanded: false,\n    };\n    let items = TreeCollection::new(vec![labeled, leaf(2, \"Banana\")]);\n    let mut service = service(props().items(items));\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::TypeaheadSearch('a'))); // matches \"Apple\" label\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(1)));\n}\n\n// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Snapshots — every anatomy part across output-affecting branches\n// ----------------------------------------------------------------------------"

427	                    ctx.expanded.set(exp);
428	                }))

pointer/programmatic focus clears it.\nfn focus_plan(key: Key, keyboard: bool) -> TransitionPlan<Machine> {\n    TransitionPlan::to(State::Focused)\n        .apply(move |ctx| { ctx.focused_node = Some(key); ctx.focus_visible = keyboard; })\n        .with_effect(PendingEffect::named(Effect::ScrollFocusedIntoView))\n}\n\n/// Keep `focused_node` on a visible node after an expansion/data change: move\n/// to the nearest visible ancestor, or clear when the node was removed.\nfn clamp_focus_to_visible(ctx: &mut Context) {\n    let Some(focused) = ctx.focused_node.clone() else { return; };\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n    if visible.contains(&focused) { return; }\n    let mut current = ctx.items.get(&focused).and_then(|n| n.parent_key.clone());\n    while let Some(ancestor) = current {\n        if visible.contains(&ancestor) { ctx.focused_node = Some(ancestor); 609	/// Next visible node whose label starts with `ch` (case-insensitive), after the
610	/// focused node, wrapping around.
611	fn typeahead_target(ctx: &Context, ch: char) -> Option<Key> {
612	    let needle = ch.to_lowercase().next().unwrap_or(ch);
613	    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);
614	    if visible.is_empty() { return None; }
615	    let start = ctx.focused_node.as_ref()
616	        .and_then(|f| visible.iter().position(|k| k == f))
617	        .map_or(0, |p| p + 1);
618	    visible.iter().cycle().skip(start).take(visible.len())
619	        .find(|key| ctx.items.get(key)
620	            .and_then(|n| n.text_value.chars().next())
621	            .map(|c| c.to_lowercase().next().unwrap_or(c)) == Some(needle))
622	        .cloned()
623	}
624	
625	/// Ordered valid keyboard drop slots for the dragged node: for every visible
626	/// node that is neither the dragged node nor a descendant of it, three slots
627	/// `Before`, `On`, `After`.
628	fn valid_drop_slots(ctx: &Context, dragging: &Key) -> Vec<CollectionDropTarget> {
629	    let mut slots = Vec::new();
630	    for key in visible_keys(ctx) {
631	        if &key == dragging || is_descendant(&ctx.items, dragging, &key) { continue; }
632	        for position in [DropPosition::Before, DropPosition::On, DropPosition::After] {
633	            slots.push(CollectionDropTarget { key: key.clone(), position });
634	        }
635	    }
636	    slots
637	}
638	
639	/// Step the keyboard drop target to the next/previous valid slot.
640	fn drag_step(ctx: &Context, props: &Props, direction: Direction) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
641	    if !props.dnd_enabled { return None; }
642	    let dragging = ctx.dragging.as_ref()?;
643	    let slots = valid_drop_slots(ctx, dragging);
644	    if slots.is_empty() { return None; }
645	    let next = match ctx.drop_target.as_ref().and_then(|c| slots.iter().position(|s| s == c)) {
646	        Some(pos) => match direction {
647	            Direction::Next => (pos + 1) % slots.len(),
648	            Direction::Prev => (pos + slots.len() - 1) % slots.len(),
649	        },
650	        None => match direction { Direction::Next => 0, Direction::Prev => slots.len() - 1 },
651	    };
652	    let target = slots[next].clone();
653	    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.drop_target = Some(target)))
654	}

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVEA
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:624  (commentId=3311549233)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-visible focus targets**

When callers use the public `focus_node` API, or an adapter dispatches a stale key, this branch accepts any key and `root_attrs` will emit `aria-activedescendant` for an id that may not exist or may be hidden under a collapsed parent. The relative-focus paths only choose visible keys and the collapse/sync paths clamp after the fact, so `FocusNode(key(5))` while its parent is collapsed (or `FocusNode(key(999))`) leaves the tree with a dangling active descendant until another corrective event happens; please gate this event through the current visible keys / collection lookup before applying `focus_plan`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVEG
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1633  (commentId=3311549239)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include lazy siblings in the `*` shortcut**

For lazy-loaded branches whose `TreeItem::has_children` is true but `Node::has_children` is still false, the node renders as expandable and `ArrowRight`/`ExpandAll` can expand it, but the `*` keyboard shortcut skips it here because it only checks the structural child flag. In a level containing lazy siblings, pressing `*` expands only already-loaded branches, leaving equally expandable lazy branches collapsed and bypassing the documented sibling-expansion behavior.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVEM
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:630  (commentId=3311549248)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Choose an active node when the tree receives focus**

When a keyboard user tabs into a fresh tree, this transition enters `State::Focused` but leaves `focused_node` as `None`, so `root_attrs` has no `aria-activedescendant` even though the focused state is defined as focus on some node. Until the user presses an arrow key, adapters have no active item to announce or pass to node-level handlers; focus should initialize to the selected item when present, otherwise the first visible node.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVER
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:797  (commentId=3311549255)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize selection after mode changes**

When an uncontrolled tree changes `selection_mode` at runtime, this rebuilds `selection_state` from the existing selected set without normalizing it for the new mode. For example, switching from multiple selection with two selected nodes to `Single` or `None` leaves both keys in `ctx.selected`, so rendered items can still expose `aria-selected="true"` even though the new configuration no longer permits that selection shape.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVEU
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:830  (commentId=3311549259)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resync generated ids when `Props::id` changes**

This prop-change check ignores `id`, and the sync path never rebuilds `ctx.ids`, so changing a TreeView's id leaves all generated node ids and `aria-activedescendant` values based on the old id. In contexts that re-key or namespace component ids after mount, the rendered `data`/ARIA relationships stay stale even after `set_props` succeeds.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVEd
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1462  (commentId=3311549271)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Make drag handles keyboard focusable**

The drag handle is exposed as `role="button"` and `on_drag_handle_keydown` is the only keyboard DnD entrypoint, but these attrs do not include `tabindex="0"`. When adapters render the handle as a non-native element, keyboard users cannot tab to it to start a drag, so the documented keyboard drag protocol is unreachable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVEl
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1677  (commentId=3311549281)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not announce disabled nodes as draggable**

With `dnd_enabled` true, disabled tree items still pass through this branch and receive `aria-roledescription="draggable"`, even though `DragStart` explicitly rejects disabled nodes. A disabled item will therefore be announced as draggable while every attempt to drag it is ignored; skip the draggable state when `disabled` is true.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVEq
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:608  (commentId=3311549292)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep controlled selection state in sync**

When `selected` is controlled, `ctx.selected.set(...)` only updates the internal fallback while `ctx.selected.get()` still returns the parent-owned value, but this branch still replaces `selection_state` with the newly selected key. If the parent does not immediately echo the change, rendered selection and the selection state machine diverge, so follow-up actions like pressing Space on the visibly selected item operate against the wrong selected set.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== THREAD PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FIVE1
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1432  (commentId=3311549303)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Suppress links on disabled nodes**

For a disabled tree item that also has an `href`, the leaf still renders a live `href`, so native anchor activation can navigate even though the node is marked `aria-disabled` and selection/drag interactions are rejected. In that disabled+href combination, omit the link target (or otherwise prevent activation) so disabled items are not still actionable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

{

  "old_string": "const fn effective_selection_mode(props: &Props) -> selection::Mode {\n    if props.multiple {\n        selection::Mode::Multiple\n    } else {\n        props.selection_mode\n    }\n}",
  "new_string": "const fn effective_selection_mode(props: &Props) -> selection::Mode {\n    if props.multiple {\n        selection::Mode::Multiple\n    } else {\n        props.selection_mode\n    }\n}\n\n/// Commit a new selection state, keeping `selection_state` consistent with what\n/// `ctx.selected.get()` reports. For uncontrolled selection that is the value\n/// just set; for controlled selection it is the parent-owned value, so the\n/// optimistic change only takes visible effect once the parent echoes it via\n/// props (avoiding a binding-vs-state divergence under controlled selection).\nfn apply_selection(ctx: &mut Context, mut new_state: selection::State) {\n    ctx.selected.set(new_state.selected_keys.clone());\n    new_state.selected_keys = ctx.selected.get().clone();\n    ctx.selection_state = new_state;\n}\n\n/// The node to activate when the tree first receives focus: the first selected\n/// visible node, otherwise the first visible node.\nfn initial_active_node(ctx: &Context) -> Option<Key> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n    let selected = ctx.selected.get();\n    visible\n        .iter()\n        .find(|&key| selected.contains(key))\n        .or_else(|| visible.first())\n        .cloned()\n}\n\n/// Reduce a selection set to one valid for `mode`: `None` clears it, `Single`\n/// keeps at most one key, `Multiple` leaves it unchanged. Applied when the\n/// effective selection mode tightens at runtime.\nfn normalize_selection(set: selection::Set, mode: selection::Mode) -> selection::Set {\n    match mode {\n        selection::Mode::None => selection::Set::Empty,\n        selection::Mode::Single => match set.first() {\n            Some(key) => selection::Set::Single(key.clone()),\n            None => selection::Set::Empty,\n        },\n        selection::Mode::Multiple => set,\n    }\n}"
}

  "old_string": "/// The effective selection mode: `multiple = true` upgrades to `Multiple` so\n/// the documented shortcut enables real multi-selection.\nconst fn effective_selection_mode(props: &Props) -> selection::Mode {\n    if props.multiple { selection::Mode::Multiple } else { props.selection_mode }\n}",
  "new_string": "/// The effective selection mode: `multiple = true` upgrades to `Multiple` so\n/// the documented shortcut enables real multi-selection.\nconst fn effective_selection_mode(props: &Props) -> selection::Mode {\n    if props.multiple { selection::Mode::Multiple } else { props.selection_mode }\n}\n\n/// Commit a new selection state, keeping `selection_state` consistent with what\n/// `ctx.selected.get()` reports (the controlled value when controlled), so the\n/// binding and the state machine never diverge under controlled selection.\nfn apply_selection(ctx: &mut Context, mut new_state: selection::State) {\n    ctx.selected.set(new_state.selected_keys.clone());\n    new_state.selected_keys = ctx.selected.get().clone();\n    ctx.selection_state = new_state;\n}\n\n/// The node to activate when the tree first receives focus: the first selected\n/// visible node, otherwise the first visible node.\nfn initial_active_node(ctx: &Context) -> Option<Key> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n    let selected = ctx.selected.get();\n    visible.iter().find(|&key| selected.contains(key)).or_else(|| visible.first()).cloned()\n}\n\n/// Reduce a selection set to one valid for `mode`: `None` clears it, `Single`\n/// keeps at most one key, `Multiple` leaves it unchanged.\nfn normalize_selection(set: selection::Set, mode: selection::Mode) -> selection::Set {\n    match mode {\n        selection::Mode::None => selection::Set::Empty,\n        selection::Mode::Single => match set.first() {\n            Some(key) => selection::Set::Single(key.clone()),\n            None => selection::Set::Empty,\n        },\n        selection::Mode::Multiple => set,\n    }\n}"
}

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FI4e-
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1395  (commentId=3311747039)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block activation on disabled branches**

When a disabled branch control is clicked, this still dispatches `ToggleNode`, and the transition does not reject disabled keys, so an item rendered with `aria-disabled="true"` can still be expanded/collapsed by the built-in activation handler. This contradicts the spec's disabled-node contract that disabled tree items block interaction, and it will be visible for any disabled parent node with children.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FI4fF
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1586  (commentId=3311747047)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid moving past expanded lazy branches**

For a node marked `TreeItem::has_children` with no loaded children, `is_branch()` is true and once the node is expanded this path sends `FocusNext`, which moves focus to the next visible sibling rather than a child. In the lazy/unloaded case there is no rendered child to enter, so ArrowRight should be inert or wait for children; otherwise keyboard users skip out of the branch just by pressing Right on an expanded placeholder.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FI4fM
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:605  (commentId=3311747055)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unknown keys before selecting**

When `SelectNode` is sent for a stale or unknown key, this path feeds it directly into `selection::State::select`, so uncontrolled state can accumulate a key that is not present in `ctx.items` and later make a newly loaded node with that key appear selected. Other paths such as `FocusNode` already gate on visible/existing keys; selection should similarly ignore keys that are not real selectable tree nodes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FI4fS
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:803  (commentId=3311747059)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear drag state when the item set changes**

If props replace `items` while a drag is active, this sync overwrites the collection but leaves `dragging` and `drop_target` untouched. When the dragged key was removed but the old target still exists, a later `Drop` passes validation and fires `on_reorder` with a bogus `source_path` containing only the removed key, so prop-driven reorders/removals during a drag can produce invalid reorder callbacks.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FI4fW
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:950  (commentId=3311747067)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use locale-aware matching for typeahead**

The TreeView spec's internationalization section requires typeahead to use locale collation when available, but this implementation compares only the first lowercased Unicode scalar. For localized labels such as accented initial letters that should collate with the typed base letter, typeahead will fail even though `Context` already carries the active locale.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FI4fb
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:560  (commentId=3311747073)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject expansion for non-branch nodes**

When `ExpandNode` or `ToggleNode` is sent for a leaf or stale key, the key is inserted into `expanded` without checking that it is an expandable branch. That makes a leaf appear expanded through `data-ars-expanded` even though it has no `aria-expanded` or children, and it leaves invalid keys in controlled/uncontrolled expansion state; expansion events should be ignored unless the key belongs to a real branch/lazy branch.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FI4fg
file: crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:816  (commentId=3311747079)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize controlled selection on mode changes**

When `selected` is controlled and `selection_mode` is changed from Multiple to Single or None, this `set(normalized)` only updates the bindable's internal value; `get()` still returns the parent-controlled multi-selection, so `selection_state` is rebuilt with a set that violates the new mode. The normalization needs to affect the value used for `selection_state`/ARIA or controlled trees can keep multiple selected nodes while advertising single/no selection.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
```

  "old_string": "/// Commit a new selection state, keeping `selection_state` consistent with what\n/// `ctx.selected.get()` reports. For uncontrolled selection that is the value\n/// just set; for controlled selection it is the parent-owned value, so the\n/// optimistic change only takes visible effect once the parent echoes it via\n/// props (avoiding a binding-vs-state divergence under controlled selection).\nfn apply_selection(ctx: &mut Context, mut new_state: selection::State) {\n    ctx.selected.set(new_state.selected_keys.clone());\n    new_state.selected_keys = ctx.selected.get().clone();\n    ctx.selection_state = new_state;\n}\n\n/// The node to activate when the tree first receives focus: the first selected\n/// visible node, otherwise the first visible node.\nfn initial_active_node(ctx: &Context) -> Option<Key> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n    let selected = ctx.selected.get();\n    visible\n        .iter()\n        .find(|&key| selected.contains(key))\n        .or_else(|| visible.first())\n        .cloned()\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Commit a new selection state. `selection_state.selected_keys` is the\n/// authoritative selection the component renders, kept consistent with the\n/// binding (`ctx.selected.get()`) and always normalized for the current mode —\n/// so controlled selection cannot diverge from the binding, and a binding that\n/// violates the mode (e.g. multiple keys under `Single`) is mode-clamped for\n/// rendering without mutating the parent-owned value.\nfn apply_selection(ctx: &mut Context, mut new_state: selection::State) {\n    ctx.selected.set(new_state.selected_keys.clone());\n    new_state.selected_keys = normalize_selection(ctx.selected.get().clone(), ctx.selection_mode);\n    ctx.selection_state = new_state;\n}\n\n/// The node to activate when the tree first receives focus: the first selected\n/// visible node, otherwise the first visible node.\nfn initial_active_node(ctx: &Context) -> Option<Key> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n    let selected = &ctx.selection_state.selected_keys;\n    visible\n        .iter()\n        .find(|&key| selected.contains(key))\n        .or_else(|| visible.first())\n        .cloned()\n}"
}

132	    /// case folding, beginning the search from the item *after* `current_focus`
133	    /// (single-char, cycling) or *at* `current_focus` (multi-char, refining).
134	    ///
135	    /// Single-character searches wrap; multi-character searches do not (they

137	    #[cfg(not(feature = "i18n"))]
138	    fn find_match<T, C: Collection<T>>(
139	        search: &str,
140	        current_focus: Option<&Key>,
141	        collection: &C,
142	        disabled_keys: &BTreeSet<Key>,
143	        disabled_behavior: DisabledBehavior,
144	    ) -> Option<Key> {
145	        // Determine single-char mode from the raw input, not the lowercased
146	        // query — one typed character can expand to multiple scalars after case

148	        let single_char = search.chars().count() == 1;
149	
150	        let query = search.to_lowercase();

152	        // FocusOnly: disabled items are focusable, so include them in the scan.

154	        let skip_disabled = disabled_behavior == DisabledBehavior::Skip;
155	
156	        let all_item_keys = collection

158	            .filter(|n| n.is_focusable() && (!skip_disabled || !disabled_keys.contains(&n.key)))

161	
162	        if all_item_keys.is_empty() {
163	            return None;
164	        }
165	
166	        // Single-char: start AFTER current_focus (cycling to next match).
167	        // Multi-char: start AT current_focus (refining keeps current match viable).
168	        let start_pos = current_focus
169	            .and_then(|k| all_item_keys.iter().position(|ik| ik == k))
170	            .map_or(0, |p| {
171	                if single_char {
172	                    (p + 1) % all_item_keys.len()
173	                } else {
174	                    p
175	                }
176	            });
177	
178	        // Single-char wraps around the full list; multi-char scans forward only.
179	        let scan_len = if single_char {
180	            all_item_keys.len()
181	        } else {
182	            all_item_keys.len().saturating_sub(start_pos)
183	        };
184	
185	        for offset in 0..scan_len {
186	            let idx = (start_pos + offset) % all_item_keys.len();
187	
188	            let key = &all_item_keys[idx];
189	
190	            if let Some(text) = collection.text_value_of(key)
191	                && text.to_lowercase().starts_with(&query)
192	            {
193	                return Some(key.clone());
194	            }
195	        }

989	    /// Map a keydown on the tree root (active descendant `node_id`) to events
990	    /// per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern (§3.2). Logical, not RTL-swapped (§3.3).
991	    pub fn on_node_keydown(&self, node_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData) {
992	        match data.key {
993	            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::FocusNext),
994	            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::FocusPrev),
995	            KeyboardKey::Home => (self.send)(Event::FocusFirst),
996	            KeyboardKey::End => (self.send)(Event::FocusLast),
997	            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => {
998	                // Branch only: expand when collapsed, else enter the first child.
999	                // On a leaf the key is inert (WAI-ARIA tree pattern).
1000	                if self.is_branch(node_id) {
1001	                    if self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {
1002	                        (self.send)(Event::FocusNext);
1003	                    } else {
1004	                        (self.send)(Event::ExpandNode(node_id.clone()));
1005	                    }
1006	                }
1007	            }
1008	            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {
1009	                if self.is_branch(node_id) && self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {
1010	                    (self.send)(Event::CollapseNode(node_id.clone()));
1011	                } else {
1012	                    (self.send)(Event::FocusParent);
1013	                }
1014	            }
1015	            // Enter selects; Space toggles (deselects when already selected).
1016	            KeyboardKey::Enter => (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone())),
1017	            KeyboardKey::Space => if self.is_node_selected(node_id) {
1018	                (self.send)(Event::DeselectNode(node_id.clone()));
1019	            } else {
1020	                (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone()));
1021	            },
1022	            _ => if let Some(ch) = data.character {
1023	                if ch == '*' { self.expand_siblings(node_id); }
1024	                else if !ch.is_control() { (self.send)(Event::TypeaheadSearch(ch)); }
1025	            },
1026	        }
1027	    }

Logical, not RTL-swapped (§3.3).\n    pub fn on_node_keydown(&self, node_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData) {\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::FocusNext),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::FocusPrev),\n            KeyboardKey::Home => (self.send)(Event::FocusFirst),\n            KeyboardKey::End => (self.send)(Event::FocusLast),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => {\n                // Branch only: expand when collapsed, else enter the first child.\n                // On a leaf the key is inert (WAI-ARIA tree pattern).\n                if self.is_branch(node_id) {\n                    if self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {\n                        (self.send)(Event::FocusNext);\n                    } else {\n                        (self.send)(Event::ExpandNode(node_id.clone()));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {\n                if self.is_branch(node_id) && self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {\n                    (self.send)(Event::CollapseNode(node_id.clone()));\n                } else {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusParent);\n                }\n            }\n            // Enter selects; Space toggles (deselects when already selected).\n            KeyboardKey::Enter => (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone())),\n            KeyboardKey::Space => if self.is_node_selected(node_id) {\n                (self.send)(Event::DeselectNode(node_id.clone()));\n            } else {\n                (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone()));\n            },\n            _ => if let Some(ch) = data.character {\n                if ch == '*' { self.expand_siblings(node_id); }\n                else if !ch.is_control() { (self.send)(Event::TypeaheadSearch(ch)); }\n            },\n        }\n    }",
  "new_string": "    /// Map a keydown on the tree root (active descendant `node_id`) to events\n    /// per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern (§3.2). Logical, not RTL-swapped (§3.3).\n    /// Uses a host/fallback clock for typeahead timing; `on_node_keydown_at`\n    /// takes an explicit adapter clock.\n    pub fn on_node_keydown(&self, node_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData) {\n        self.on_node_keydown_impl(node_id, data, None);\n    }\n\n    /// `on_node_keydown` with an explicit `now_ms` for typeahead timing.\n    pub fn on_node_keydown_at(&self, node_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData, now_ms: u64) {\n        self.on_node_keydown_impl(node_id, data, Some(now_ms));\n    }\n\n    fn on_node_keydown_impl(&self, node_id: &Key, data: &KeyboardEventData, now_ms: Option<u64>) {\n        match data.key {\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowDown => (self.send)(Event::FocusNext),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowUp => (self.send)(Event::FocusPrev),\n            KeyboardKey::Home => (self.send)(Event::FocusFirst),\n            KeyboardKey::End => (self.send)(Event::FocusLast),\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowRight => {\n                // Branch only. Collapsed -> expand. Expanded with loaded children\n                // -> enter first child. A leaf, or an expanded lazy branch with no\n                // rendered children, is inert (WAI-ARIA tree pattern).\n                if self.is_branch(node_id) {\n                    if !self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {\n                        (self.send)(Event::ExpandNode(node_id.clone()));\n                    } else if self.has_loaded_children(node_id) {\n                        (self.send)(Event::FocusNext);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            KeyboardKey::ArrowLeft => {\n                if self.is_branch(node_id) && self.is_node_expanded(node_id) {\n                    (self.send)(Event::CollapseNode(node_id.clone()));\n                } else {\n                    (self.send)(Event::FocusParent);\n                }\n            }\n            // Enter selects; Space toggles (deselects when already selected).\n            KeyboardKey::Enter => (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone())),\n            KeyboardKey::Space => if self.is_node_selected(node_id) {\n                (self.send)(Event::DeselectNode(node_id.clone()));\n            } else {\n                (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone()));\n            },\n            _ => if let Some(ch) = data.character {\n                if ch == '*' { self.expand_siblings(node_id); }\n                else if !ch.is_control() {\n                    (self.send)(Event::TypeaheadSearch(ch, typeahead_time(now_ms, &self.ctx.typeahead)));\n                }\n            },\n        }\n    }"
}
