=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FKIF_
crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:675 (cid=3312191747)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Clear stale typeahead state on blur**

When the tree blurs after a printable-key search, this transition only clears `focus_visible`; if the user refocuses within the 500 ms typeahead timeout, the next printable key is appended to the old buffer instead of starting a fresh search. The component already exposes `ClearTypeahead` for blur/reset, so this should reset `ctx.typeahead` here to avoid cross-focus-session searches.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FKIGB
crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1370 (cid=3312191752)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve keyboard modality on root focus**

The standard connect handler always sends `is_keyboard: false`, so when a user tabs into the tree through the wired `on_root_focus` path the active descendant is initialized but `focus_visible` remains false and the focused treeitem never gets `data-ars-focus-visible` until another navigation key is pressed. This should either accept/pass focus modality or otherwise avoid hard-coding pointer modality for all root focus events.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FKIGD
crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:529 (cid=3312191754)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep disabled tree items reachable by typeahead**

`TreeItem::disabled` documents that disabled nodes remain focusable, and arrow navigation still includes them, but this selection state is left with the default `DisabledBehavior::Skip`; `process_typeahead` forwards that behavior to the shared matcher, which filters disabled keys out. In a tree with a disabled item whose label matches the typed prefix, typeahead will skip a focusable node and jump to a later match or no match, so TreeView should configure disabled behavior as focus-only while still preventing selection/drag.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FKIGG
crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:905 (cid=3312191758)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resync when drag-and-drop is disabled**

Because `dnd_enabled` is omitted from the prop-change check, turning DnD off while a drag is active does not dispatch `SyncProps`, so `ctx.dragging` and `ctx.drop_target` can remain set indefinitely even though subsequent drag/drop events are rejected by `props.dnd_enabled`. Include this prop in the sync condition so the existing `SyncProps` cleanup path clears stale drag state when the feature is disabled at runtime.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FKIGH
crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:1585 (cid=3312191761)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Disable drag handles for disabled nodes**

For a disabled node in a DnD-enabled tree, `drag_handle_attrs` still returns a focusable button with an active drag label even though `DragStart` rejects disabled nodes. If adapters render handles for each item in the DnD variant, keyboard and screen-reader users get an operable-looking control that cannot do anything; the handle should be suppressed or marked disabled/non-focusable for disabled items.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FKIGL
crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:980 (cid=3312191764)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match typeahead against the current expansion state**

`process_typeahead` passes the raw `TreeCollection` to the shared matcher, whose `nodes()` iterator uses the collection's own expansion snapshot rather than `ctx.expanded`. After a user expands or collapses a branch through TreeView, focus/navigation and rendering use `visible_keys_with_expanded(ctx.expanded)`, but typeahead still searches the original visibility set, so it can skip newly visible children or jump to nodes hidden by a TreeView collapse.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

=== PRRT_kwDORp4enM6FKIGO
crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs:765 (cid=3312191769)
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject nested drag starts**

If a drag is already active, another `DragStart` currently overwrites `ctx.dragging` and clears the existing drop target, so pressing another handle or receiving a second pointer-start mid-drag silently switches the source item instead of preserving/canceling the active drag. Guard `DragStart` when `ctx.dragging.is_some()` so an in-flight reorder cannot be retargeted without an explicit drop or cancel.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

  "new_string": "/// Advance the shared typeahead matcher by one character. Delegates to the\n/// canonical [`typeahead::State`] (multi-character buffer with timeout reset and\n/// locale-aware collation/case-folding when the `i18n` feature is enabled),\n/// matching against the collection's `text_value`.\n///\n/// The matcher scans the collection's own visible set, so the collection is\n/// first reconciled to the component's live `ctx.expanded` — otherwise typeahead\n/// would search the construction-time expansion and skip newly-visible children\n/// (or jump to nodes the user has since collapsed).\nfn process_typeahead(ctx: &Context, ch: char, now_ms: u64) -> (typeahead::State, Option<Key>) {\n    let items = reconciled_items(ctx);\n    ctx.typeahead.process_char_with_locale(\n        ch,\n        now_ms,\n        ctx.focused_node.as_ref(),\n        &items,\n        &ctx.locale,\n        &ctx.selection_state.disabled_keys,\n        ctx.selection_state.disabled_behavior,\n    )\n}\n\n/// `ctx.items` with its internal expansion reconciled to the live `ctx.expanded`\n/// set, so the collection's visible iteration matches what the tree renders.\nfn reconciled_items(ctx: &Context) -> TreeCollection<TreeItem> {\n    let expanded = ctx.expanded.get();\n    let mut items = ctx.items.clone();\n    let branch_keys = items\n        .all_nodes()\n        .filter(|node| node.has_children)\n        .map(|node| node.key.clone())\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    for key in branch_keys {\n        let want = expanded.contains(&key);\n        if items.is_expanded(&key) != want {\n            items = items.set_expanded(&key, want);\n        }\n    }\n    items\n}"
}

typing 'a' must still reach it\n    // (FocusOnly), even though it remains non-selectable.\n    let mut service = service(props().items(disabled_items()));\n    drop(service.send(Event::TypeaheadSearch('a', 1)));\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(2)));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn disabling_dnd_at_runtime_clears_active_drag() {\n    let mut service = service(dnd_props());\n    drop(service.send(Event::DragStart(key(2))));\n    assert_eq!(service.context().dragging, Some(key(2)));\n\n    drop(service.set_props(props())); // dnd_enabled = false\n    assert_eq!(service.context().dragging, None);\n    assert_eq!(service.context().drop_target, None);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn disabled_node_drag_handle_is_not_operable() {\n    let service = service(props().items(disabled_items()).dnd_enabled(true));\n    let attrs = service.connect(&|_| {}).drag_handle_attrs(&key(2)); // Apple disabled\n    assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled)), Some(\"true\"));\n    assert_eq!(attrs.get(&HtmlAttr::TabIndex), Some(\"-1\"));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn typeahead_respects_live_expansion_state() {\n    // Vegetables (4) starts collapsed (Carrot hidden).   "old_string": "/// Advance the shared typeahead matcher by one character. Delegates to the\n/// canonical `ars_collections::typeahead::State` (multi-character buffer with\n/// timeout reset and locale-aware collation/case-folding when the `i18n`\n/// feature is enabled), matching the collection's `text_value` and skipping\n/// disabled nodes.\nfn process_typeahead(ctx: &Context, ch: char, now_ms: u64) -> (typeahead::State, Option<Key>) {\n    ctx.typeahead.process_char_with_locale(\n        ch,\n        now_ms,\n        ctx.focused_node.as_ref(),\n        &ctx.items,\n        &ctx.locale,\n        &ctx.selection_state.disabled_keys,\n        ctx.selection_state.disabled_behavior,\n    )\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Advance the shared typeahead matcher by one character. Delegates to the\n/// canonical `ars_collections::typeahead::State` (multi-character buffer with\n/// timeout reset and locale-aware collation/case-folding when the `i18n`\n/// feature is enabled), matching the collection's `text_value`. Disabled nodes\n/// stay reachable because the selection state uses `DisabledBehavior::FocusOnly`.\n///\n/// The matcher scans the collection's own visible set, so the collection is\n/// first reconciled to the component's live `ctx.expanded` — otherwise typeahead\n/// would search the construction-time expansion and skip newly-visible children\n/// (or jump to nodes the user has since collapsed).\nfn process_typeahead(ctx: &Context, ch: char, now_ms: u64) -> (typeahead::State, Option<Key>) {\n    let items = reconciled_items(ctx);\n    ctx.typeahead.process_char_with_locale(\n        ch,\n        now_ms,\n        ctx.focused_node.as_ref(),\n        &items,\n        &ctx.locale,\n        &ctx.selection_state.disabled_keys,\n        ctx.selection_state.disabled_behavior,\n    )\n}\n\n/// `ctx.items` with its internal expansion reconciled to the live `ctx.expanded`\n/// set, so the collection's visible iteration matches what the tree renders.\nfn reconciled_items(ctx: &Context) -> TreeCollection<TreeItem> {\n    let expanded = ctx.expanded.get();\n    let mut items = ctx.items.clone();\n    let branch_keys = items.all_nodes()\n        .filter(|node| node.has_children)\n        .map(|node| node.key.clone())\n        .collect::<Vec<_>>();\n    for key in branch_keys {\n        let want = expanded.contains(&key);\n        if items.is_expanded(&key) != want {\n            items = items.set_expanded(&key, want);\n        }\n    }\n    items\n}"
}

  "new_string": "    pub fn drag_handle_attrs(&self, node_id: &Key) -> AttrMap {\n        let mut attrs = part_only_attrs(&Part::DragHandle { node_id: Key::default() });\n        let item = self.ctx.items.get(node_id).and_then(|n| n.value.as_ref());\n        let disabled = item.is_some_and(|v| v.disabled);\n        let label = item.map_or(\"\", |v| v.label.as_str());\n        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, \"button\")\n            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), (self.ctx.messages.drag_handle_label)(label, &self.ctx.locale));\n        if disabled {\n            // A disabled node cannot be dragged (`DragStart` rejects it), so the\n            // handle is marked disabled and removed from the tab sequence rather\n            // than presenting an operable-looking control.\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), \"true\").set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, \"-1\");\n        } else {\n            // `tabindex=\"0\"` so keyboard users can tab to the handle to start a drag.\n            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, \"0\");\n            if self.is_dragging(node_id) { attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Grabbed), \"true\"); }\n        }\n        attrs\n    }"

1400	> **Drag and Drop Reorder**: When `dnd_enabled: true` is set, TreeView surfaces the agnostic drag-and-drop reorder logic — the `DragHandle` and `DropIndicator` anatomy parts (canonical bare names, per `06-collections.md` §10.8 and the listbox/gridlist/table specs), the drag-state events, valid drop-slot enumeration, cycle-free drop validation, and `ReorderEvent` path computation. It reports completion through `Props::on_reorder` driven by the named `Effect::Reorder`. Dropping **between** siblings uses `DropPosition::Before`/`After`; dropping **onto** a node to reparent uses `DropPosition::On`. The collection-level `DraggableCollection<T>` / `DroppableCollection<T>` trait impls (which bundle the live `selection::State`), pointer hit-testing, the 500 ms hover-expand timer, and `use_drag`/`use_drop` DOM wiring are **adapter** concerns (tracked by the TreeView Leptos/Dioxus adapter tasks), not part of this agnostic core.
1401	
1402	### 4.2 Drag-Reorder Behavior
1403	
1404	When drag-and-drop reorder is enabled (`dnd_enabled: true`), the following behaviors apply. The
1405	**agnostic core** owns the data-model logic (slot enumeration, validity, paths, attrs, keyboard
1406	protocol); pointer hit-testing and the hover-expand timer are **adapter**-resolved.
1407	
1408	- **Drag handle**: Each tree item renders an optional drag handle affordance (the `DragHandle`
1409	  anatomy part). The handle is the grab target; the entire row is not draggable by default to
1410	  avoid conflicts with text selection. `drag_handle_attrs` emits `role="button"` and a localized
1411	  `aria-label` from `Messages::drag_handle_label`, plus `aria-grabbed="true"` while dragging.
1412	- **Hover-expand** (adapter): When the pointer dwells over a collapsed node during a drag, the
1413	  adapter expands it after a 500 ms hover delay by sending `ExpandNode`. The agnostic core has no
1414	  timer.
1415	- **Drop target indication**: The `DropIndicator` part marks the current drop slot with
1416	  `data-ars-drop-position` (`before` / `on` / `after`) and `data-ars-drop-target` (the target
1417	  node's id). Three drop positions are supported:
1418	  - `DropPosition::Before` — insert before the target node (horizontal line above)
1419	  - `DropPosition::After` — insert after the target node (horizontal line below)
1420	  - `DropPosition::On` — reparent as a child of the target node (target background highlight)
1421	- **Drop position detection** (adapter): The adapter maps the pointer's vertical position within
1422	  the target row — top 25% = `Before`, bottom 25% = `After`, middle 50% = `On` — to a
1423	  `CollectionDropTarget` and sends `DragOver`.
1424	- **Keyboard drag** (agnostic core, via `on_drag_handle_keydown`):
1425	  - `Enter` / `Space` on a focused drag handle picks up the item (`DragStart`).
1426	  - Arrow Up/Down step the item through the valid drop slots (`DragMovePrev` / `DragMoveNext`).
1427	  - `Enter` confirms the drop (`Drop`).
1428	  - `Escape` cancels and discards the drop target (`CancelDrag`).
1429	- **Drop validity**: The core rejects dropping a node onto itself or any of its descendants
1430	  (cycle prevention) in both `DragOver` and `Drop`.
1431	- **Reorder callback**: `Props::on_reorder: Option<Callback<ReorderEvent>>` fires when a drop is
1432	  completed. The core never mutates `ctx.items`; the consumer applies the reorder to its data
1433	  source and re-supplies props (pure-notification, like Tabs).
1434

1151	
1152	    slots
1153	}
1154	
1155	/// Step the keyboard drop target to the next/previous valid slot.
1156	fn drag_step(
1157	    ctx: &Context,
1158	    props: &Props,
1159	    direction: Direction,
1160	) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
1161	    if !props.dnd_enabled {
1162	        return None;
1163	    }
1164	
1165	    let dragging = ctx.dragging.as_ref()?;
1166	
1167	    let slots = valid_drop_slots(ctx, dragging);
1168	
1169	    if slots.is_empty() {
1170	        return None;
1171	    }
1172	
1173	    let next = if let Some(pos) = ctx
1174	        .drop_target
1175	        .as_ref()
1176	        .and_then(|current| slots.iter().position(|slot| slot == current))
1177	    {
1178	        match direction {
1179	            Direction::Next => (pos + 1) % slots.len(),
1180	            Direction::Prev => (pos + slots.len() - 1) % slots.len(),
1181	        }
1182	    } else {
1183	        match direction {
1184	            Direction::Next => 0,
1185	            Direction::Prev => slots.len() - 1,
1186	        }
1187	    };
1188	
1189	    let target = slots[next].clone();
1190	
1191	    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
1192	        ctx.drop_target = Some(target);
1193	    }))
1194	}

1196	/// Whether `candidate` is `ancestor` itself or sits below it in the tree.
1197	fn is_descendant(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, ancestor: &Key, candidate: &Key) -> bool {
1198	    let mut current = items
1199	        .get(candidate)
1200	        .and_then(|node| node.parent_key.clone());
1201	
1202	    while let Some(parent) = current {
1203	        if &parent == ancestor {
1204	            return true;
1205	        }
1206	
1207	        current = items.get(&parent).and_then(|node| node.parent_key.clone());
1208	    }
1209	
1210	    false
1211	}
1212	
1213	/// Whether `key` is a node that expand/collapse may act on: it exists, is an
1214	/// expandable branch (real children or the lazy `has_children` flag), and is
1215	/// not disabled (disabled nodes block all interaction).
1216	fn is_interactive_branch(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, key: &Key) -> bool {
1217	    items.get(key).is_some_and(|node| {
1218	        let item = node.value.as_ref();
1219	        let expandable = node.has_children || item.is_some_and(|item| item.has_children);
1220	        let disabled = item.is_some_and(|item| item.disabled);
1221	        expandable && !disabled
1222	    })
1223	}
1224	
1225	/// Whether dropping the dragged node at `target` is valid: the target must be a
1226	/// real node in the collection (adapters can send stale/unknown keys during
1227	/// pointer hit-testing), and never the dragged node itself or any of its
1228	/// descendants (which would create a cycle).
1229	fn is_valid_drop(
1230	    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,
1231	    dragging: &Key,
1232	    target: &CollectionDropTarget,
1233	) -> bool {
1234	    items.get(&target.key).is_some()
1235	        && &target.key != dragging
1236	        && !is_descendant(items, dragging, &target.key)
1237	}
1238	
1239	/// The path of keys from the root down to `key` (inclusive).
1240	fn path_to(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, key: &Key) -> Vec<Key> {
1241	    let mut path = Vec::new();
1242	    let mut current = Some(key.clone());
1243	
1244	    while let Some(node_key) = current {
1245	        current = items
1246	            .get(&node_key)
1247	            .and_then(|node| node.parent_key.clone());
1248	
1249	        path.push(node_key);
1250	    }
1251	
1252	    path.reverse();
1253	
1254	    path
1255	}

1257	/// Build the named reorder effect that invokes [`Props::on_reorder`].
1258	fn reorder_effect(event: ReorderEvent) -> PendingEffect<Machine> {
1259	    PendingEffect::new(

1261	        move |_ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {
1262	            if let Some(callback) = &props.on_reorder {
1263	                callback(event.clone());
1264	            }
1265	
1266	            no_cleanup()
1267	        },
1268	    )
1269	}

50	    Multiple(BTreeSet<Key>),
51	
52	    /// All items are selected.
53	    All,
54	}
55	
56	impl Set {
57	    /// Returns `true` when `key` is part of this selection.
58	    #[must_use]
59	    pub fn contains(&self, key: &Key) -> bool {
60	        match self {
61	            Self::Empty => false,
62	            Self::Single(selected) => selected == key,
63	            Self::Multiple(selected) => selected.contains(key),
64	            Self::All => true,
65	        }
66	    }
67	
68	    /// Returns `true` when no items are selected.
69	    #[must_use]
70	    pub const fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
71	        matches!(self, Self::Empty)
72	    }
73	
74	    /// Returns `true` when all items are selected.
75	    #[must_use]
76	    pub const fn is_all(&self) -> bool {
77	        matches!(self, Self::All)
78	    }
79	
80	    /// Returns the first selected key when one is available.
81	    #[must_use]
82	    pub fn first(&self) -> Option<&Key> {
83	        match self {
84	            Self::Single(key) => Some(key),
85	            Self::Multiple(keys) => keys.first(),
86	            Self::Empty | Self::All => None,
87	        }
88	    }
89	
90	    /// Returns the number of selected items, or `None` for `All`.
91	    #[must_use]
92	    pub fn count(&self) -> Option<usize> {
93	        match self {
94	            Self::Empty => Some(0),
95	            Self::Single(_) => Some(1),
96	            Self::Multiple(keys) => Some(keys.len()),
97	            Self::All => None,
98	        }
99	    }
100	
101	    /// Returns the number of selected items.
102	    ///
103	    /// `All` returns `0`; callers that need to distinguish that case should
104	    /// prefer [`Self::count`].
105	    #[must_use]
106	    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
107	        self.count().unwrap_or(0)
108	    }
109	
110	    /// Iterates over the selected keys.
111	    ///
112	    /// `All` returns an empty iterator because it must be resolved against a
113	    /// concrete collection.
114	    #[must_use]
115	    pub fn keys(&self) -> Box<dyn Iterator<Item = &Key> + '_> {
116	        match self {
117	            Self::Empty | Self::All => Box::new(core::iter::empty()),
118	            Self::Single(key) => Box::new(core::iter::once(key)),
119	            Self::Multiple(keys) => Box::new(keys.iter()),
120	        }
121	    }
122	}

124	/// Controls how disabled items behave in selection contexts.
125	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
126	#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
127	pub enum DisabledBehavior {
128	    /// Disabled items are skipped during keyboard navigation.
129	    #[default]
130	    Skip,
131	
132	    /// Disabled items are focusable but not selectable.
133	    FocusOnly,
134	}
135	
136	/// Callback for item action (Enter, double-click, tap in replace mode).
137	///
138	/// Distinct from selection change: action activates the item associated with
139	/// the provided [`Key`].
140	pub type OnAction = Option<Callback<dyn Fn(Key) + Send + Sync>>;
141

143	#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]
144	#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
145	pub struct State {

148	
149	    /// The anchor for range selection.
150	    pub anchor_key: Option<Key>,
151	
152	    /// The item that currently has focus.
153	    pub focused_key: Option<Key>,
154	
155	    /// Keys that are disabled and excluded from selection operations.
156	    pub disabled_keys: BTreeSet<Key>,

160	
161	    /// Selection mode for this instance.

163	
164	    /// Selection behavior for this instance.
165	    pub behavior: Behavior,
166	
167	    /// Whether touch-based selection mode is currently active.
168	    pub selection_mode_active: bool,
169

  "old_string": "/// Resolve the relative focus target, wrapping at the ends.\nfn focus_relative(ctx: &Context, direction: Direction) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n\n    if visible.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let target = if let Some(current) = &ctx.focused_node\n        && let Some(pos) = visible.iter().position(|key| key == current)\n    {\n        match direction {\n            Direction::Next => visible.get(pos + 1).or_else(|| visible.first()),\n            Direction::Prev => {\n                if pos > 0 {\n                    visible.get(pos - 1)\n                } else {\n                    visible.last()\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    } else {\n        match direction {\n            Direction::Next => visible.first(),\n            Direction::Prev => visible.last(),\n        }\n    };\n\n    target.cloned().map(|key| focus_plan(key, true))\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Resolve the relative focus target. Per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, Down/Up\n/// move to the next/previous visible node and **do not wrap** at the ends\n/// (Home/End jump to the boundaries); a step past the last/first node is a\n/// no-op.\nfn focus_relative(ctx: &Context, direction: Direction) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n\n    if visible.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let target = if let Some(current) = &ctx.focused_node\n        && let Some(pos) = visible.iter().position(|key| key == current)\n    {\n        match direction {\n            Direction::Next => visible.get(pos + 1),\n            Direction::Prev => pos.checked_sub(1).and_then(|prev| visible.get(prev)),\n        }\n    } else {\n        // No prior focus: enter at the near end for the travel direction.\n        match direction {\n            Direction::Next => visible.first(),\n            Direction::Prev => visible.last(),\n        }\n    };\n\n    target.cloned().map(|key| focus_plan(key, true))\n}"
}

{

  "file_path": "/Users/ericson/Workspace/Rust/ars-ui.worktrees/task-267/crates/ars-components/src/navigation/tree_view/mod.rs",
  "old_string": "/// Whether dropping the dragged node at `target` is valid: the target must be a\n/// real node in the collection (adapters can send stale/unknown keys during\n/// pointer hit-testing), and never the dragged node itself or any of its\n/// descendants (which would create a cycle).\nfn is_valid_drop(\n    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,\n    dragging: &Key,\n    target: &CollectionDropTarget,\n) -> bool {\n    items.get(&target.key).is_some()\n        && &target.key != dragging\n        && !is_descendant(items, dragging, &target.key)\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Whether dropping the dragged node at `target` is valid: the target must be a\n/// currently **visible** node (adapters can send stale keys for rows hidden\n/// under a collapsed parent during pointer hit-testing or virtualization), and\n/// never the dragged node itself or any of its descendants (which would create\n/// a cycle). `visible` is the live visible-key set (`visible_keys`).\nfn is_valid_drop(\n    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,\n    visible: &[Key],\n    dragging: &Key,\n    target: &CollectionDropTarget,\n) -> bool {\n    visible.contains(&target.key)\n        && &target.key != dragging\n        && !is_descendant(items, dragging, &target.key)\n}\n\n/// Whether `key` is a node the user may pick up to drag: it exists, is\n/// focusable, and is not disabled (disabled nodes block all interaction).\nfn is_draggable(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, key: &Key) -> bool {\n    let node = items.get(key);\n    node.is_some_and(Node::is_focusable)\n        && !node\n            .and_then(|node| node.value.as_ref())\n            .is_some_and(|item| item.disabled)\n}\n\n/// Whether `key` names a node that can actually be selected: it exists in the\n/// collection and is not disabled. Used to keep the rendered selection free of\n/// removed or disabled keys.\nfn is_selectable_key(\n    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,\n    disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>,\n    key: &Key,\n) -> bool {\n    items.get(key).is_some() && !disabled.contains(key)\n}\n\n/// Drop selection keys that cannot be selected in `items` (missing or disabled\n/// nodes), then normalize the remainder for `mode`. Applied at init and on every\n/// `SyncProps` so the rendered selection (and the uncontrolled binding) can\n/// never report a removed or disabled node as selected.\nfn sanitize_selection(\n    set: selection::Set,\n    mode: selection::Mode,\n    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,\n    disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>,\n) -> selection::Set {\n    let retained = match set {\n        // `All` is symbolic and never produced by TreeView; pass it through.\n        selection::Set::Empty | selection::Set::All => set,\n        selection::Set::Single(key) => {\n            if is_selectable_key(items, disabled, &key) {\n                selection::Set::Single(key)\n            } else {\n                selection::Set::Empty\n            }\n        }\n        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {\n            let kept = keys\n                .into_iter()\n                .filter(|key| is_selectable_key(items, disabled, key))\n                .collect::<BTreeSet<Key>>();\n            if kept.is_empty() {\n                selection::Set::Empty\n            } else {\n                selection::Set::Multiple(kept)\n            }\n        }\n    };\n\n    normalize_selection(retained, mode)\n}"
}

  "old_string": "#[test]\nfn focus_next_skips_collapsed_children_and_wraps() {\n    let mut service = service(props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNode(key(4)))); // Vegetables (collapsed)\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNext));\n\n    // Carrot/Daikon are hidden; next visible after Vegetables is Grains.\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(7)));\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNext)); // wraps to first\n\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(1)));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn focus_prev_wraps_to_last() {\n    let mut service = service(props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusFirst));\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusPrev));\n\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(7)));\n}",
  "new_string": "#[test]\nfn focus_next_skips_collapsed_children_and_stops_at_end() {\n    let mut service = service(props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNode(key(4)))); // Vegetables (collapsed)\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNext));\n\n    // Carrot/Daikon are hidden; next visible after Vegetables is Grains.\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(7)));\n\n    // Per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, ArrowDown does not wrap: at the last node\n    // it is a no-op (Home/End handle boundary jumps), so focus stays on Grains.\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusNext));\n\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(7)));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn focus_prev_at_first_node_does_not_wrap() {\n    let mut service = service(props());\n\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusFirst));\n    drop(service.send(Event::FocusPrev)); // ArrowUp at the first node is a no-op.\n\n    assert_eq!(service.context().focused_node, Some(key(1)));\n}"
}

  "old_string": "/// Relative focus target, wrapping at the ends.\nfn focus_relative(ctx: &Context, direction: Direction) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n    if visible.is_empty() { return None; }\n    let target = match ctx.focused_node.as_ref()\n        .and_then(|current| visible.iter().position(|k| k == current))\n    {\n        Some(pos) => match direction {\n            Direction::Next => visible.get(pos + 1).or_else(|| visible.first()),\n            Direction::Prev => if pos > 0 { visible.get(pos - 1) } else { visible.last() },\n        },\n        None => match direction { Direction::Next => visible.first(), Direction::Prev => visible.last() },\n    };\n    target.cloned().map(|k| focus_plan(k, true))\n}",
  "new_string": "/// Relative focus target. Per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, Down/Up move to the\n/// next/previous visible node and **do not wrap** at the ends (Home/End jump to\n/// the boundaries); a step past the last/first node is a no-op.\nfn focus_relative(ctx: &Context, direction: Direction) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let visible = visible_keys(ctx);\n    if visible.is_empty() { return None; }\n    let target = match ctx.focused_node.as_ref()\n        .and_then(|current| visible.iter().position(|k| k == current))\n    {\n        Some(pos) => match direction {\n            Direction::Next => visible.get(pos + 1),\n            Direction::Prev => pos.checked_sub(1).and_then(|prev| visible.get(prev)),\n        },\n        // No prior focus: enter at the near end for the travel direction.\n        None => match direction { Direction::Next => visible.first(), Direction::Prev => visible.last() },\n    };\n    target.cloned().map(|k| focus_plan(k, true))\n}"
}

760	/// Resolve the timestamp for a typeahead keypress: the adapter-provided value
761	/// when present, else the host clock (std), else a monotonic bump of the last
762	/// keypress so the buffer never spuriously resets.
763	fn typeahead_time(now_ms: Option<u64>, state: &typeahead::State) -> u64 {
764	    now_ms.unwrap_or_else(|| current_time_ms().unwrap_or(state.last_key_time_ms.saturating_add(1)))
765	}

767	/// Ordered valid keyboard drop slots for the dragged node: for every visible
768	/// node that is neither the dragged node nor a descendant of it, three slots
769	/// `Before`, `On`, `After`.
770	fn valid_drop_slots(ctx: &Context, dragging: &Key) -> Vec<CollectionDropTarget> {
771	    let mut slots = Vec::new();
772	    for key in visible_keys(ctx) {
773	        if &key == dragging || is_descendant(&ctx.items, dragging, &key) { continue; }
774	        for position in [DropPosition::Before, DropPosition::On, DropPosition::After] {
775	            slots.push(CollectionDropTarget { key: key.clone(), position });
776	        }
777	    }
778	    slots
779	}
780	
781	/// Step the keyboard drop target to the next/previous valid slot.
782	fn drag_step(ctx: &Context, props: &Props, direction: Direction) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
783	    if !props.dnd_enabled { return None; }
784	    let dragging = ctx.dragging.as_ref()?;
785	    let slots = valid_drop_slots(ctx, dragging);
786	    if slots.is_empty() { return None; }
787	    let next = match ctx.drop_target.as_ref().and_then(|c| slots.iter().position(|s| s == c)) {
788	        Some(pos) => match direction {
789	            Direction::Next => (pos + 1) % slots.len(),
790	            Direction::Prev => (pos + slots.len() - 1) % slots.len(),
791	        },
792	        None => match direction { Direction::Next => 0, Direction::Prev => slots.len() - 1 },
793	    };
794	    let target = slots[next].clone();
795	    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.drop_target = Some(target)))
796	}

  "old_string": "/// A drop is valid when the target is a real node (adapters can send stale or\n/// unknown keys during pointer hit-testing) and is not the dragged node or one\n/// of its descendants (which would create a cycle).\nfn is_valid_drop(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, dragging: &Key, target: &CollectionDropTarget) -> bool {\n    items.get(&target.key).is_some()\n        && &target.key != dragging\n        && !is_descendant(items, dragging, &target.key)\n}",
  "new_string": "/// A drop is valid when the target is a currently **visible** node (adapters can\n/// send stale keys for rows hidden under a collapsed parent during pointer\n/// hit-testing or virtualization) and is not the dragged node or one of its\n/// descendants (which would create a cycle). `visible` is the live visible-key\n/// set (`visible_keys`).\nfn is_valid_drop(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, visible: &[Key], dragging: &Key, target: &CollectionDropTarget) -> bool {\n    visible.contains(&target.key)\n        && &target.key != dragging\n        && !is_descendant(items, dragging, &target.key)\n}\n\n/// Whether `key` is a node the user may pick up to drag: it exists, is\n/// focusable, and is not disabled (disabled nodes block all interaction).\nfn is_draggable(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, key: &Key) -> bool {\n    let node = items.get(key);\n    node.is_some_and(Node::is_focusable)\n        && !node.and_then(|n| n.value.as_ref()).is_some_and(|i| i.disabled)\n}\n\n/// Whether `key` names a node that can be selected: it exists and is not\n/// disabled. Keeps the rendered selection free of removed or disabled keys.\nfn is_selectable_key(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>, key: &Key) -> bool {\n    items.get(key).is_some() && !disabled.contains(key)\n}\n\n/// Drop selection keys that cannot be selected in `items` (missing or disabled\n/// nodes), then normalize the remainder for `mode`. Applied at init and on every\n/// `SyncProps` so the rendered selection (and the uncontrolled binding) can\n/// never report a removed or disabled node as selected. The symbolic `All` and\n/// any future `#[non_exhaustive]` `Set` variant pass through unfiltered.\nfn sanitize_selection(set: selection::Set, mode: selection::Mode, items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>) -> selection::Set {\n    let retained = match set {\n        selection::Set::Single(key) =>\n            if is_selectable_key(items, disabled, &key) { selection::Set::Single(key) } else { selection::Set::Empty },\n        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {\n            let kept = keys.into_iter().filter(|k| is_selectable_key(items, disabled, k)).collect::<BTreeSet<Key>>();\n            if kept.is_empty() { selection::Set::Empty } else { selection::Set::Multiple(kept) }\n        }\n        other => other,\n    };\n    normalize_selection(retained, mode)\n}"
}

Reads the mode-normalized selection state so\n    /// rendering never exposes a selection shape the current mode forbids.\n    pub fn is_node_selected(&self, node_id: &Key) -> bool {\n        self.ctx.selection_state.selected_keys.contains(node_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether a node with the given `disabled` flag can be selected: selection\n    /// must be enabled (`selection_mode != None`) and the node must be enabled.\n    /// Non-selectable nodes omit `aria-selected` per the WAI-ARIA tree pattern.\n    fn is_node_selectable(&self, disabled: bool) -> bool {\n        !disabled && !matches!(self.ctx.selection_mode, selection::Mode::None)\n    }\n\n    /// Whether a node is expanded.\n    pub fn is_node_expanded(&self, node_id: &Key) -> bool {\n        self.ctx.expanded.get().contains(node_id)\n    }"

1118	        let mut attrs = part_only_attrs(&Part::DragHandle { node_id: Key::default() });
1119	        let item = self.ctx.items.get(node_id).and_then(|n| n.value.as_ref());
1120	        let disabled = item.is_some_and(|v| v.disabled);
1121	        let label = item.map_or("", |v| v.label.as_str());
1122	        attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Role, "button")
1123	            .set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Label), (self.ctx.messages.drag_handle_label)(label, &self.ctx.locale));
1124	        if disabled {
1125	            // A disabled node cannot be dragged (`DragStart` rejects it), so the
1126	            // handle is marked disabled and removed from the tab sequence rather
1127	            // than presenting an operable-looking control.
1128	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Disabled), "true").set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, "-1");
1129	        } else {
1130	            // `tabindex="0"` so keyboard users can tab to the handle to start a drag.
1131	            attrs.set(HtmlAttr::TabIndex, "0");
1132	            if self.is_dragging(node_id) { attrs.set(HtmlAttr::Aria(AriaAttr::Grabbed), "true"); }
1133	        }
1134	        attrs
1135	    }

1366	### 3.1 ARIA Roles, States, and Properties
1367	
1368	| Part            | Role       | Properties                                                                                                                                                                |
1369	| --------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1370	| `Root`          | `tree`     | `aria-multiselectable="true"` when `multiple=true`                                                                                                                        |
1371	| `Branch`        | `treeitem` | `aria-expanded="true\|false"` (emitted when node has children or `has_children` is true), `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset` |
1372	| `BranchContent` | `group`    | —                                                                                                                                                                         |
1373	| `Leaf`          | `treeitem` | `aria-selected`, `aria-disabled`, `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, `aria-posinset`. When `has_children` is true: also `aria-expanded="false"`                                |
1374	
1375	When a tree item has an `href`, the adapter renders the clickable area (`BranchControl` or
1376	`Leaf`) as an `<a>` element. The `role="treeitem"` on the parent `Branch`/`Leaf` container is
1377	preserved — the `<a>` is a descendant of the `role="treeitem"` element, not a replacement for
1378	it. This allows native link semantics (middle-click, Ctrl+click) while maintaining the ARIA tree
1379	pattern.
1380	
1381	`aria-level` reflects DOM nesting depth (1-based). `aria-setsize` and `aria-posinset` enable
1382	screen readers to announce "item 3 of 5" when navigating.
1383	
1384	**Parent-child ARIA relationships:** The DOM hierarchy is sufficient to establish parent-child
1385	relationships — `aria-owns` is NOT used because children are rendered as direct DOM descendants
1386	of their parent treeitem. Branch children are wrapped in a `BranchContent` element with
1387	`role="group"` (see anatomy table above), which groups the child treeitems under the parent

1409	### 3.3 RTL Navigation Semantics
1410	
1411	`TreeView` keyboard navigation uses **logical** (not visual) semantics that remain consistent regardless of text direction. In both LTR and RTL layouts:
1412	
1413	- **ArrowRight / ArrowDown** = expand a collapsed branch, or navigate to the first child of an expanded branch.
1414	- **ArrowLeft / ArrowUp** = collapse an expanded branch, or navigate to the parent node.
1415	
1416	This matches the WAI-ARIA `TreeView` pattern, where ArrowRight/ArrowLeft map to expand/collapse (parent-child hierarchy), not to visual direction. The adapter does **not** swap ArrowLeft/ArrowRight in RTL mode for `TreeView`, unlike flat list components (`Accordion`, `Tabs`) where arrows map to next/previous sibling. The rationale is that tree hierarchy is a logical relationship independent of layout direction.
1417	
1418	### 3.4 Selection Announcements
1419	
1420	- Selected items have `aria-selected="true"` (already present)
1421	- Selection changes are announced via focus movement to the selected node
1422	- For programmatic selection changes (no focus change), use LiveAnnouncer:
1423	  `announce("{item label} selected", "polite")`

1488	
1489	> **Drag and Drop Reorder**: When `dnd_enabled: true` is set, TreeView surfaces the agnostic drag-and-drop reorder logic — the `DragHandle` and `DropIndicator` anatomy parts (canonical bare names, per `06-collections.md` §10.8 and the listbox/gridlist/table specs), the drag-state events, valid drop-slot enumeration, cycle-free drop validation, and `ReorderEvent` path computation. It reports completion through `Props::on_reorder` driven by the named `Effect::Reorder`. Dropping **between** siblings uses `DropPosition::Before`/`After`; dropping **onto** a node to reparent uses `DropPosition::On`. The collection-level `DraggableCollection<T>` / `DroppableCollection<T>` trait impls (which bundle the live `selection::State`), pointer hit-testing, the 500 ms hover-expand timer, and `use_drag`/`use_drop` DOM wiring are **adapter** concerns (tracked by the TreeView Leptos/Dioxus adapter tasks), not part of this agnostic core.
1490	
1491	### 4.2 Drag-Reorder Behavior
1492	
1493	When drag-and-drop reorder is enabled (`dnd_enabled: true`), the following behaviors apply. The
1494	**agnostic core** owns the data-model logic (slot enumeration, validity, paths, attrs, keyboard
1495	protocol); pointer hit-testing and the hover-expand timer are **adapter**-resolved.
1496	
1497	- **Drag handle**: Each tree item renders an optional drag handle affordance (the `DragHandle`
1498	  anatomy part). The handle is the grab target; the entire row is not draggable by default to
1499	  avoid conflicts with text selection. `drag_handle_attrs` emits `role="button"` and a localized
1500	  `aria-label` from `Messages::drag_handle_label`, plus `aria-grabbed="true"` while dragging. For a
1501	  **disabled** node the handle is non-operable: `DragStart` rejects it, so `drag_handle_attrs` emits
1502	  `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"` (removed from the tab sequence, no `aria-grabbed`)
1503	  rather than presenting an operable-looking control.
1504	- **Hover-expand** (adapter): When the pointer dwells over a collapsed node during a drag, the
1505	  adapter expands it after a 500 ms hover delay by sending `ExpandNode`. The agnostic core has no
1506	  timer.
1507	- **Drop target indication**: The `DropIndicator` part marks the current drop slot with
1508	  `data-ars-drop-position` (`before` / `on` / `after`) and `data-ars-drop-target` (the target
1509	  node's id). Three drop positions are supported:
1510	  - `DropPosition::Before` — insert before the target node (horizontal line above)
1511	  - `DropPosition::After` — insert after the target node (horizontal line below)
1512	  - `DropPosition::On` — reparent as a child of the target node (target background highlight)
1513	- **Drop position detection** (adapter): The adapter maps the pointer's vertical position within
1514	  the target row — top 25% = `Before`, bottom 25% = `After`, middle 50% = `On` — to a
1515	  `CollectionDropTarget` and sends `DragOver`.
1516	- **Keyboard drag** (agnostic core, via `on_drag_handle_keydown`):
1517	  - `Enter` / `Space` on a focused drag handle picks up the item (`DragStart`).
1518	  - Arrow Up/Down step the item through the valid drop slots (`DragMovePrev` / `DragMoveNext`).
1519	  - `Enter` confirms the drop (`Drop`).
1520	  - `Escape` cancels and discards the drop target (`CancelDrag`).
1521	- **Single in-flight drag**: `DragStart` is rejected while a drag is already active (`ctx.dragging`
1522	  is set), so a second handle pickup or a stray pointer-start cannot silently retarget the source
1523	  node — the active drag must be confirmed (`Drop`) or cancelled (`CancelDrag`) first.
1524	- **Runtime disable**: Setting `dnd_enabled: false` while a drag is in flight resyncs via
1525	  `SyncProps`, which clears `ctx.dragging` / `ctx.drop_target` so no stale drag state lingers once
1526	  the feature is turned off.
1527	- **Drop validity**: The core rejects dropping a node onto itself or any of its descendants
1528	  (cycle prevention) in both `DragOver` and `Drop`.
1529	- **Reorder callback**: `Props::on_reorder: Option<Callback<ReorderEvent>>` fires when a drop is
1530	  completed. The core never mutates `ctx.items`; the consumer applies the reorder to its data
1531	  source and re-supplies props (pure-notification, like Tabs).
1532

  "new_string": "- **Single in-flight drag**: `DragStart` is rejected while a drag is already active (`ctx.dragging`\n  is set), so a second handle pickup or a stray pointer-start cannot silently retarget the source\n  node — the active drag must be confirmed (`Drop`) or cancelled (`CancelDrag`) first.\n- **Drag survives unrelated prop echoes**: a `SyncProps` triggered by a non-item prop change\n  (`expanded`, `selected`, `id`, selection config) does **not** cancel an in-flight drag. The core\n  re-validates instead: it discards the drag only when DnD is turned off, the item collection itself\n  changed (paths now stale), or the dragged/target keys are no longer valid (a target hidden by a\n  collapsed parent is dropped while the pickup is preserved). This keeps a controlled-expanded tree's\n  hover-expand `expanded` echo from breaking a reorder.\n- **Drop validity**: A valid drop target must be a currently **visible** node (a row hidden under a\n  collapsed parent is rejected, since pointer hit-testing can send stale keys during\n  collapse/virtualization) and never the dragged node itself or one of its descendants (cycle\n  prevention). This is enforced in both `DragOver` and `Drop`. When `DragOver` reports an **invalid**\n  target during an active drag, any previously-set `ctx.drop_target` is **cleared** so a later `Drop`\n  cannot fire against a slot the user is no longer indicating."
}

**Round 5 — 8 P2 findings, all fixed (commit 293150df, pushed to PR #695):**

| # | Finding | Fix | Regression test(s) |
|---|---------|-----|-----|
| R5-1 | Disabled key in initial selection rendered as selected | `sanitize_selection` filters disabled/missing keys in init + SyncProps | `disabled_initial_selection_is_dropped` |
| R5-2 | Non-selectable nodes still emitted `aria-selected` | `is_node_selectable` gate in branch/leaf attrs | `non_selectable_nodes_omit_aria_selected` |
| R5-3 | Arrow nav wrapped at boundaries | `focus_relative` no-wrap (APG tree pattern) | `focus_next_..._stops_at_end`, `focus_prev_at_first_node_does_not_wrap` |
| R5-4 | Stale `drop_target` survived an invalid hover | `DragOver` clears target on invalid slot | `drag_over_invalid_target_clears_stale_drop_target` |
| R5-5 | Drag handle operable when DnD off | `inert` covers `!dnd_enabled` too | `drag_handle_is_inert_when_dnd_disabled` |
| R5-6 | Drag cancelled by unrelated prop echoes | SyncProps re-validates instead of blanket-cancelling | `expansion_prop_echo_preserves_active_drag`, `stale_drop_target_cleared_when_echo_hides_it` |
| R5-7 | Drop accepted onto rows hidden under collapsed parents | `is_valid_drop` requires target in live visible set | `drag_over_hidden_target_is_rejected` |
| R5-8 | Removed keys lingered in selection | `sanitize_selection` drops absent keys on resync | `selection_drops_keys_removed_from_collection`, `multiple_selection_drops_all_removed_keys` |

**One thing worth flagging:** R5-3 reverses the earlier deliberate wrap-around design. I implemented the no-wrap behavior because it's directly mandated by the W3C WAI-ARIA APG tree pattern (Down/Up move to next/previous, Home/End jump to boundaries) and matches the Zag/React Aria parity targets. If you had a specific reason for wrapping, let me know and I can revisit.

  "new_string": "fn is_valid_drop(\n    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,\n    visible: &[Key],\n    dragging: &Key,\n    target: &CollectionDropTarget,\n) -> bool {\n    visible.contains(&target.key)\n        && &target.key != dragging\n        && !is_disabled_node(items, &target.key)\n        && !is_descendant(items, dragging, &target.key)\n}\n\n/// Whether `key` names a disabled node (disabled nodes block all interaction, so\n/// they are never valid drag sources or drop targets).\nfn is_disabled_node(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, key: &Key) -> bool {\n    items\n        .get(key)\n        .and_then(|node| node.value.as_ref())\n        .is_some_and(|item| item.disabled)\n}"
}

1330	/// `SyncProps` so the rendered selection (and the uncontrolled binding) can
1331	/// never report a removed or disabled node as selected.
1332	fn sanitize_selection(
1333	    set: selection::Set,
1334	    mode: selection::Mode,
1335	    items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>,
1336	    disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>,
1337	) -> selection::Set {
1338	    let retained = match set {
1339	        selection::Set::Single(key) => {
1340	            if is_selectable_key(items, disabled, &key) {
1341	                selection::Set::Single(key)
1342	            } else {
1343	                selection::Set::Empty
1344	            }
1345	        }
1346	        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {
1347	            let kept = keys
1348	                .into_iter()
1349	                .filter(|key| is_selectable_key(items, disabled, key))
1350	                .collect::<BTreeSet<Key>>();
1351	            if kept.is_empty() {
1352	                selection::Set::Empty
1353	            } else {
1354	                selection::Set::Multiple(kept)
1355	            }
1356	        }
1357	        // `Empty`, the symbolic `All` (never produced by TreeView), and any
1358	        // future `#[non_exhaustive]` variant pass through unfiltered.
1359	        other => other,
1360	    };

Resolve it to the concrete selectable keys present in the\n        // collection so it cannot bypass the disabled/missing filtering.\n        selection::Set::All => {\n            let kept = items\n                .all_keys()\n                .filter(|key| !disabled.contains(key))\n                .cloned()\n                .collect::<BTreeSet<Key>>();\n            if kept.is_empty() {\n                selection::Set::Empty\n            } else {\n                selection::Set::Multiple(kept)\n            }\n        }\n        // `Empty` and any future `#[non_exhaustive]` variant pass through.\n        other => other,\n    };"

#[test]
fn keydown_arrows_navigate() {
    let service = service(props());

    assert_eq!(
        dispatch_key(&service, &key(1), &keyboard(KeyboardKey::ArrowDown)),
        &[Event::FocusNext]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        dispatch_key(&service, &key(1), &keyboard(KeyboardKey::ArrowUp)),
        &[Event::FocusPrev]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        dispatch_key(&service, &key(1), &keyboard(KeyboardKey::Home)),
        &[Event::FocusFirst]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        dispatch_key(&service, &key(1), &keyboard(KeyboardKey::End)),
        &[Event::FocusLast]
    );
}

#[test]
fn keydown_arrow_right_expands_collapsed_branch_else_enters() {
    let service = service(props());

    // Vegetables (4) is a collapsed branch -> expand it.
    assert_eq!(
        dispatch_key(&service, &key(4), &keyboard(KeyboardKey::ArrowRight)),
        &[Event::ExpandNode(key(4))]
    );
    // Fruits (1) is already expanded -> enter (move to next visible).
    assert_eq!(
        dispatch_key(&service, &key(1), &keyboard(KeyboardKey::ArrowRight)),
        &[Event::FocusNext]
    );
    // A leaf -> inert (nothing to expand or enter; WAI-ARIA tree pattern).
    assert!(dispatch_key(&service, &key(7), &keyboard(KeyboardKey::ArrowRight)).is_empty());
}

781	/// `ctx.items` with its internal expansion reconciled to the live `ctx.expanded`
782	/// set, so the collection's visible iteration matches what the tree renders.
783	fn reconciled_items(ctx: &Context) -> TreeCollection<TreeItem> {
784	    let expanded = ctx.expanded.get();
785	    let mut items = ctx.items.clone();
786	    let branch_keys = items.all_nodes()
787	        .filter(|node| node.has_children)
788	        .map(|node| node.key.clone())
789	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
790	    for key in branch_keys {
791	        let want = expanded.contains(&key);
792	        if items.is_expanded(&key) != want {
793	            items = items.set_expanded(&key, want);
794	        }
795	    }
796	    items
797	}

799	/// Resolve the timestamp for a typeahead keypress: the adapter-provided value
800	/// when present, else the host clock (std), else a monotonic bump of the last
801	/// keypress so the buffer never spuriously resets.
802	fn typeahead_time(now_ms: Option<u64>, state: &typeahead::State) -> u64 {
803	    now_ms.unwrap_or_else(|| current_time_ms().unwrap_or(state.last_key_time_ms.saturating_add(1)))
804	}

806	/// Ordered valid keyboard drop slots for the dragged node: for every visible
807	/// node that is neither the dragged node nor a descendant of it, three slots
808	/// `Before`, `On`, `After`.
809	fn valid_drop_slots(ctx: &Context, dragging: &Key) -> Vec<CollectionDropTarget> {
810	    let mut slots = Vec::new();
811	    for key in visible_keys(ctx) {
812	        if &key == dragging || is_descendant(&ctx.items, dragging, &key) { continue; }
813	        for position in [DropPosition::Before, DropPosition::On, DropPosition::After] {
814	            slots.push(CollectionDropTarget { key: key.clone(), position });
815	        }
816	    }
817	    slots
818	}

820	/// Step the keyboard drop target to the next/previous valid slot.
821	fn drag_step(ctx: &Context, props: &Props, direction: Direction) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {
822	    if !props.dnd_enabled { return None; }
823	    let dragging = ctx.dragging.as_ref()?;
824	    let slots = valid_drop_slots(ctx, dragging);
825	    if slots.is_empty() { return None; }
826	    let next = match ctx.drop_target.as_ref().and_then(|c| slots.iter().position(|s| s == c)) {
827	        Some(pos) => match direction {
828	            Direction::Next => (pos + 1) % slots.len(),
829	            Direction::Prev => (pos + slots.len() - 1) % slots.len(),
830	        },
831	        None => match direction { Direction::Next => 0, Direction::Prev => slots.len() - 1 },
832	    };
833	    let target = slots[next].clone();
834	    Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx| ctx.drop_target = Some(target)))
835	}

861	/// A drop is valid when the target is a currently **visible** node (adapters can
862	/// send stale keys for rows hidden under a collapsed parent during pointer
863	/// hit-testing or virtualization) and is not the dragged node or one of its
864	/// descendants (which would create a cycle). `visible` is the live visible-key
865	/// set (`visible_keys`).
866	fn is_valid_drop(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, visible: &[Key], dragging: &Key, target: &CollectionDropTarget) -> bool {
867	    visible.contains(&target.key)
868	        && &target.key != dragging
869	        && !is_descendant(items, dragging, &target.key)
870	}
871	
872	/// Whether `key` is a node the user may pick up to drag: it exists, is
873	/// focusable, and is not disabled (disabled nodes block all interaction).
874	fn is_draggable(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, key: &Key) -> bool {
875	    let node = items.get(key);
876	    node.is_some_and(Node::is_focusable)
877	        && !node.and_then(|n| n.value.as_ref()).is_some_and(|i| i.disabled)
878	}
879	
880	/// Whether `key` names a node that can be selected: it exists and is not
881	/// disabled. Keeps the rendered selection free of removed or disabled keys.
882	fn is_selectable_key(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>, key: &Key) -> bool {
883	    items.get(key).is_some() && !disabled.contains(key)
884	}
885	
886	/// Drop selection keys that cannot be selected in `items` (missing or disabled
887	/// nodes), then normalize the remainder for `mode`. Applied at init and on every
888	/// `SyncProps` so the rendered selection (and the uncontrolled binding) can
889	/// never report a removed or disabled node as selected. The symbolic `All` and
890	/// any future `#[non_exhaustive]` `Set` variant pass through unfiltered.
891	fn sanitize_selection(set: selection::Set, mode: selection::Mode, items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>) -> selection::Set {
892	    let retained = match set {
893	        selection::Set::Single(key) =>
894	            if is_selectable_key(items, disabled, &key) { selection::Set::Single(key) } else { selection::Set::Empty },
895	        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {
896	            let kept = keys.into_iter().filter(|k| is_selectable_key(items, disabled, k)).collect::<BTreeSet<Key>>();
897	            if kept.is_empty() { selection::Set::Empty } else { selection::Set::Multiple(kept) }
898	        }
899	        other => other,
900	    };
901	    normalize_selection(retained, mode)
902	}

904	/// Path of keys from the root down to `key` (inclusive).
905	fn path_to(items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, key: &Key) -> Vec<Key> {
906	    let mut path = Vec::new();
907	    let mut current = Some(key.clone());
908	    while let Some(node_key) = current {
909	        current = items.get(&node_key).and_then(|n| n.parent_key.clone());
910	        path.push(node_key);
911	    }
912	    path.reverse();

Applied at init and on every\n/// `SyncProps` so the rendered selection (and the uncontrolled binding) can\n/// never report a removed or disabled node as selected. The symbolic `All` is\n/// resolved to the concrete selectable keys so it cannot bypass the filtering;\n/// any future `#[non_exhaustive]` `Set` variant passes through unfiltered.\nfn sanitize_selection(set: selection::Set, mode: selection::Mode, items: &TreeCollection<TreeItem>, disabled: &BTreeSet<Key>) -> selection::Set {\n    let retained = match set {\n        selection::Set::Single(key) =>\n            if is_selectable_key(items, disabled, &key) { selection::Set::Single(key) } else { selection::Set::Empty },\n        selection::Set::Multiple(keys) => {\n            let kept = keys.into_iter().filter(|k| is_selectable_key(items, disabled, k)).collect::<BTreeSet<Key>>();\n            if kept.is_empty() { selection::Set::Empty } else { selection::Set::Multiple(kept) }\n        }\n        // `Set::All`'s `contains` returns true for every key (including disabled\n        // or absent ones); resolve it to the concrete selectable keys present.\n        selection::Set::All => {\n            let kept = items.all_keys().filter(|k| !disabled.contains(k)).cloned().collect::<BTreeSet<Key>>();\n            if kept.is_empty() { selection::Set::Empty } else { selection::Set::Multiple(kept) }\n        }\n        other => other,\n    };\n    normalize_selection(retained, mode)\n}"

```
1533	- **Drag handle**: Each tree item renders an optional drag handle affordance (the `DragHandle`
1534	  anatomy part). The handle is the grab target; the entire row is not draggable by default to
1535	  avoid conflicts with text selection. `drag_handle_attrs` emits `role="button"` and a localized
1536	  `aria-label` from `Messages::drag_handle_label`, plus `aria-grabbed="true"` while dragging. The
1537	  handle is **inert** — `aria-disabled="true"` and `tabindex="-1"` (removed from the tab sequence,
1538	  no `aria-grabbed`) — for a **disabled** node (`DragStart` rejects it) and whenever DnD is off
1539	  (`on_drag_handle_keydown` no-ops), so a consumer that always renders handles never exposes an
1540	  operable-looking control that cannot perform its announced action.
1541	- **Hover-expand** (adapter): When the pointer dwells over a collapsed node during a drag, the
1542	  adapter expands it after a 500 ms hover delay by sending `ExpandNode`. The agnostic core has no
1543	  timer.
1544	- **Drop target indication**: The `DropIndicator` part marks the current drop slot with
1545	  `data-ars-drop-position` (`before` / `on` / `after`) and `data-ars-drop-target` (the target
1546	  node's id). Three drop positions are supported:
1547	  - `DropPosition::Before` — insert before the target node (horizontal line above)
1548	  - `DropPosition::After` — insert after the target node (horizontal line below)
1549	  - `DropPosition::On` — reparent as a child of the target node (target background highlight)
1550	- **Drop position detection** (adapter): The adapter maps the pointer's vertical position within
1551	  the target row — top 25% = `Before`, bottom 25% = `After`, middle 50% = `On` — to a
1552	  `CollectionDropTarget` and sends `DragOver`.
1553	- **Keyboard drag** (agnostic core, via `on_drag_handle_keydown`):
1554	  - `Enter` / `Space` on a focused drag handle picks up the item (`DragStart`).
1555	  - Arrow Up/Down step the item through the valid drop slots (`DragMovePrev` / `DragMoveNext`).
1556	  - `Enter` confirms the drop (`Drop`).
1557	  - `Escape` cancels and discards the drop target (`CancelDrag`).
1558	- **Single in-flight drag**: `DragStart` is rejected while a drag is already active (`ctx.dragging`
1559	  is set), so a second handle pickup or a stray pointer-start cannot silently retarget the source
1560	  node — the active drag must be confirmed (`Drop`) or cancelled (`CancelDrag`) first.
1561	- **Drag survives unrelated prop echoes**: a `SyncProps` triggered by a non-item prop change
1562	  (`expanded`, `selected`, `id`, selection config) does **not** cancel an in-flight drag. The core
1563	  re-validates instead: it discards the drag only when DnD is turned off, the item collection itself
1564	  changed (paths now stale), or the dragged/target keys are no longer valid (a target hidden by a
1565	  collapsed parent is dropped while the pickup is preserved). This keeps a controlled-expanded tree's
1566	  hover-expand `expanded` echo from breaking a reorder.
1567	- **Drop validity**: A valid drop target must be a currently **visible** node (a row hidden under a
1568	  collapsed parent is rejected, since pointer hit-testing can send stale keys during
1569	  collapse/virtualization) and never the dragged node itself or one of its descendants (cycle
1570	  prevention). This is enforced in both `DragOver` and `Drop`. When `DragOver` reports an **invalid**
1571	  target during an active drag, any previously-set `ctx.drop_target` is **cleared** so a later `Drop`
1572	  cannot fire against a slot the user is no longer indicating.
1573	- **Reorder callback**: `Props::on_reorder: Option<Callback<ReorderEvent>>` fires when a drop is
1574	  completed. The core never mutates `ctx.items`; the consumer applies the reorder to its data
1575	  source and re-supplies props (pure-notification, like Tabs).
1576	
1577	```rust

13://! - [`BindableValue`] — marker trait for values usable with [`Bindable`]
147:/// [`BindableValue`].
469:// Bindable
472:/// Trait alias-style marker for values usable with [`Bindable`].
476:pub trait BindableValue: Clone + PartialEq + Debug {}
478:impl<T: Clone + PartialEq + Debug> BindableValue for T {}
482:/// Components that support two-way binding use `Bindable` to distinguish between
483:/// values owned by the parent ([`controlled`](Bindable::controlled)) and values
484:/// managed by the component itself ([`uncontrolled`](Bindable::uncontrolled)).
=== Bindable impl ===
pub struct Bindable<T: BindableValue> {
    /// The externally controlled value, or `None` if uncontrolled.
    controlled: Option<T>,

    /// The internal value managed by the component.
    internal: T,
}

impl<T: BindableValue> Bindable<T> {
    /// Creates a controlled bindable owned by the parent.
    ///
    /// Both the controlled and internal fields are initialized to the given value.
    /// The component reads the controlled value via [`get`](Self::get).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn controlled(value: T) -> Self {
        Self {
            internal: value.clone(),
            controlled: Some(value),
        }
    }

    /// Creates an uncontrolled bindable managed by the component.
    ///
    /// There is no external controlled value; [`get`](Self::get) returns the
    /// internal value which can be updated via [`set`](Self::set).
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn uncontrolled(default: T) -> Self {
        Self {
            controlled: None,
            internal: default,
        }
    }

    /// Returns a reference to the current value.
    ///
    /// Returns the controlled value if set, otherwise the internal value.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn get(&self) -> &T {
        self.controlled.as_ref().unwrap_or(&self.internal)
    }

    /// Returns `true` if this value is controlled by the parent.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn is_controlled(&self) -> bool {
        self.controlled.is_some()
    }

    /// Updates the internal value.
    ///
    /// In controlled mode, this becomes the pending internal value that is
    /// revealed once the bindable returns to uncontrolled mode.
    pub fn set(&mut self, value: T) {
        self.internal = value;
    }

    /// Pushes a new controlled value from the parent.
    ///
    /// This should be called when the parent's controlled prop changes.
    pub fn sync_controlled(&mut self, value: Option<T>) {
        self.controlled = value;
    }

    /// Returns a mutable reference to the internal value.
    ///
    /// Use for in-place mutations on collection types to avoid cloning.
    /// **Warning:** For controlled bindables, mutating the internal value has no
    /// effect on what [`get`](Self::get) returns (it returns the controlled value).
    pub const fn get_mut_owned(&mut self) -> &mut T {
        &mut self.internal
    }
}

impl<T: BindableValue + Default> Default for Bindable<T> {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::uncontrolled(T::default())
    }
}

///
/// Adapters use this contract to read and replace component IDs without knowing the
/// concrete props type. The `#[derive(HasId)]` macro implements this trait for any
/// struct with a `pub id: String` field.
pub trait HasId: Sized {
    /// Returns the current DOM ID.
    fn id(&self) -> &str;

    /// Returns a copy of `self` with the DOM ID replaced.
    #[must_use]
    fn with_id(self, id: String) -> Self;

=== Effect enum ===
pub enum Effect {
    /// Adapter must scroll the active-descendant node ([`Context::focused_node`])
    /// into view. The agnostic core never moves DOM focus itself; the tree uses
    /// the active-descendant pattern, so only scrolling is adapter-resolved.
    ScrollFocusedIntoView,

    /// Adapter invokes [`Props::on_reorder`] with the completed [`ReorderEvent`].
    Reorder,
}

/// Emitted when a tree node is reordered via drag-and-drop.
///
/// Paths are sequences of keys from the root to the item, so consumers can
/// apply the reorder against their hierarchical data source without resolving
/// flat indices.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ReorderEvent {
    /// Path of the dragged node (root → node).
    pub source_path: Vec<Key>,

    /// Path of the drop target node (root → target).

571	        event: &Event,
572	        ctx: &Context,
573	        props: &Props,
574	    ) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Self>> {
575	        match event {
576	            // Expand/collapse/toggle only act on a real, enabled, expandable
577	            // branch — never a leaf, a disabled node (interaction is blocked),
578	            // or a stale/unknown key (which would otherwise leave invalid keys
579	            // in the expansion set or mark a leaf `data-ars-expanded`).
580	            Event::ExpandNode(key) => {
581	                if !is_interactive_branch(&ctx.items, key) {
582	                    return None;
583	                }
584	                let key = key.clone();
585	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
586	                    let mut expanded = ctx.expanded.get().clone();
587	
588	                    expanded.insert(key);
589	
590	                    ctx.expanded.set(expanded);
591	                }))
592	            }
593	
594	            Event::CollapseNode(key) => {
595	                if !is_interactive_branch(&ctx.items, key) {
596	                    return None;
597	                }
598	                let key = key.clone();
599	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
600	                    let mut expanded = ctx.expanded.get().clone();
601	
602	                    expanded.remove(&key);
603	
604	                    ctx.expanded.set(expanded);
605	                    // The focused node may now be hidden under the collapsed
606	                    // branch; keep `aria-activedescendant` pointing at a
607	                    // rendered element.
608	                    clamp_focus_to_visible(ctx);
609	                }))
610	            }
611	
612	            Event::ToggleNode(key) => {
613	                if !is_interactive_branch(&ctx.items, key) {
614	                    return None;
615	                }
616	                let is_expanded = ctx.expanded.get().contains(key);
617	                let key = key.clone();
618	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
619	                    let mut expanded = ctx.expanded.get().clone();
620	
621	                    if is_expanded {
622	                        expanded.remove(&key);
623	                    } else {
624	                        expanded.insert(key);
625	                    }
626	
627	                    ctx.expanded.set(expanded);
628	                    clamp_focus_to_visible(ctx);
629	                }))
630	            }
631	
632	            Event::SelectNode(key) => {
633	                // Ignore the event in non-selectable mode or for a stale/unknown
634	                // key, so selection never accumulates keys absent from `items`.
635	                if ctx.selection_mode == selection::Mode::None
636	                    || !ctx.items.get(key).is_some_and(Node::is_focusable)
637	                {
638	                    return None;
639	                }
640	
641	                let key = key.clone();
642	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
643	                    let new_state = ctx.selection_state.select(key);
644	                    apply_selection(ctx, new_state);
645	                }))
646	            }
647	
648	            Event::DeselectNode(key) => {
649	                let key = key.clone();
650	                Some(TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {
651	                    let new_state = ctx.selection_state.deselect(&key);
652	                    apply_selection(ctx, new_state);
653	                }))
654	            }
655	
656	            // Pointer / programmatic focus: do not force the keyboard focus
657	            // ring (modality is not keyboard). Only focus a node that is
658	            // currently visible, so the active descendant never dangles.
659	            Event::FocusNode(key) => {
660	                if !visible_keys(ctx).contains(key) {
661	                    return None;
662	                }
663	                Some(focus_plan(key.clone(), false))
664	            }

  "old_string": "fn apply_selection(ctx: &mut Context, mut new_state: selection::State) {\n    ctx.selected.set(new_state.selected_keys.clone());\n    new_state.selected_keys = normalize_selection(ctx.selected.get().clone(), ctx.selection_mode);\n    ctx.selection_state = new_state;\n}",
  "new_string": "fn apply_selection(ctx: &mut Context, mut new_state: selection::State) {\n    ctx.selected.set(new_state.selected_keys.clone());\n    new_state.selected_keys = normalize_selection(ctx.selected.get().clone(), ctx.selection_mode);\n    ctx.selection_state = new_state;\n}\n\n/// Build the transition for a requested selection change, following the\n/// controlled/uncontrolled bindable contract (mirrors `checkbox_group`): always\n/// notify the parent via [`Effect::SelectionChange`], but only optimistically\n/// render (commit the binding + `selection_state`) when **uncontrolled** — a\n/// controlled parent owns `Props::selected` and echoes the requested value back,\n/// so the rendered selection must not change until that echo arrives. Returns\n/// `None` (no transition) when the requested selection equals the current one.\nfn selection_change_plan(\n    ctx: &Context,\n    new_state: selection::State,\n) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    let next = normalize_selection(new_state.selected_keys.clone(), ctx.selection_mode);\n    if ctx.selected.get() == &next {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let effect = selection_change_effect(next);\n\n    if ctx.selected.is_controlled() {\n        return Some(\n            TransitionPlan::new()\n                .apply(|_: &mut Context| {})\n                .with_effect(effect),\n        );\n    }\n\n    Some(\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| apply_selection(ctx, new_state))\n            .with_effect(effect),\n    )\n}\n\n/// Build the transition for a requested expansion change. `clamp` re-clamps\n/// focus after a collapse (a now-hidden focused node must not dangle). Same\n/// controlled/uncontrolled contract as [`selection_change_plan`]: notify via\n/// [`Effect::ExpandedChange`], commit the binding only when uncontrolled.\nfn expanded_change_plan(\n    ctx: &Context,\n    next: BTreeSet<Key>,\n    clamp: bool,\n) -> Option<TransitionPlan<Machine>> {\n    if ctx.expanded.get() == &next {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    let effect = expanded_change_effect(next.clone());\n\n    if ctx.expanded.is_controlled() {\n        return Some(\n            TransitionPlan::new()\n                .apply(|_: &mut Context| {})\n                .with_effect(effect),\n        );\n    }\n\n    Some(\n        TransitionPlan::context_only(move |ctx: &mut Context| {\n            ctx.expanded.set(next);\n            if clamp {\n                clamp_focus_to_visible(ctx);\n            }\n        })\n        .with_effect(effect),\n    )\n}\n\n/// Named effect that invokes [`Props::on_selection_change`] with the requested\n/// selection set so a controlled parent can echo it back.\nfn selection_change_effect(next: selection::Set) -> PendingEffect<Machine> {\n    PendingEffect::new(\n        Effect::SelectionChange,\n        move |_ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {\n            if let Some(callback) = &props.on_selection_change {\n                callback(next.clone());\n            }\n\n            no_cleanup()\n        },\n    )\n}\n\n/// Named effect that invokes [`Props::on_expanded_change`] with the requested\n/// expanded-key set so a controlled parent can echo it back.\nfn expanded_change_effect(next: BTreeSet<Key>) -> PendingEffect<Machine> {\n    PendingEffect::new(\n        Effect::ExpandedChange,\n        move |_ctx: &Context, props: &Props, _send| {\n            if let Some(callback) = &props.on_expanded_change {\n                callback(next.clone());\n            }\n\n            no_cleanup()\n        },\n    )\n}"
}

  "new_string": "    /// Handle activation of a leaf node: select (or toggle) and focus.\n    ///\n    /// Under the default `Toggle` selection behavior, clicking an\n    /// already-selected leaf **deselects** it (mirroring the keyboard Space path\n    /// and the shared collection toggle contract). `Replace` behavior always\n    /// (re)selects, since a click replaces the current selection.\n    pub fn on_leaf_click(&self, node_id: &Key) {\n        if self.is_toggle_behavior() && self.is_node_selected(node_id) {\n            (self.send)(Event::DeselectNode(node_id.clone()));\n        } else {\n            (self.send)(Event::SelectNode(node_id.clone()));\n        }\n        (self.send)(Event::FocusNode(node_id.clone()));\n    }\n\n    /// Whether the tree uses `Toggle` selection behavior (clicks toggle), as\n    /// opposed to `Replace` (clicks replace the selection).\n    const fn is_toggle_behavior(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self.props.selection_behavior, selection::Behavior::Toggle)\n    }"
}
